articles.title: Lando Norris, impactado con el McLaren W1: "Me da un poco de miedo de lo rápido que es"
articles.standfirst: El campeón del mundo de F1 prueba el último hypercar de calle de McLaren... y se sorprende con sus prestaciones
articles.summary: El campeón del mundo de F1 prueba el último hypercar de calle de McLaren... y se sorprende con sus prestaciones
articles.body: Lando Norris está demostrando ser un auténtico 'hombre McLaren'. No sólo le ha devuelto el título mundial de F1 a la escudería británica después de 17 años o está colaborando en el desarrollo del nuevo Hypercar británico para Le Mans. También se ha 'mojado' con el último superdeportivo de calle salido de las entrañas de Woking: el W1. Un coche que, curiosamente, le debe -en parte- el nombre al propio Lando Norris ya que la W es de 'World Champions' (una estirpe de la que el joven británico es el último miembro), y que ahora ha conocido de primera mano en el circuito portugués de Portimao (precisamete la misma pista en la que probó el Hypercar papaya). Hablamos de una bestia híbrida de 1.275 caballos de potencia, con capacidad para alcanzar los 350 km/h y con un precio de 2 millones de libras... que no ha echado atrás a los multimillonarios del planeta, porque las 399 piezas que se van a crear ya están asignadas (dos de ellos, para los dos pilotos de McLaren, él y Óscar Piastri). Lo primero que hizo Norris al salir a pista fue, lógicamente, seleccionar el modo manual del cambio para tener el control total del vehículo. Dos cosas sorprendieron al británico: el agarre en curva ("tengo mucho más grip del que esperaba", reconocía) y la gran velocidad que despliega el heredero de los F1 y P1. No es extraño si tenemos en cuenta que combina un propulsor 4.0 V8 de gasolina con 915 caballos con otro eléctrico de otros 342 que transmiten su potencia únicamente a las ruedas traseras, como sucede en los monoplazas de F1. La aerodinámica activa (en especial el espectacular alerón trasero móvil Active Long Tail, que se combina con alas móviles delante) genera hasta 350 kg de apoyo delantero y 650 sobre el trasero. Normal que Norris sienta el agarre en la rapidísima de derechas en bajada de entrada a meta en la pista portuguesa. "Me duele el cuerpo porque tengo que agarrarme muy fuerte. Espero que la gente esté preparada para esto porque...", decía, profundamente impresionado. Hasta el punto de que lanzó una sugerencia para los que, como él, se atrevan a ponerse a sus mandos: "Me daba un poco de miedo de lo rápido que era. Creo que se necesitaría un permiso de conducir especial para llevarlo, una licencia de supercars o algo así". De hecho, el mejor veredicto llega en su frase final: "Estoy deseando tener el mío".

articles.title: If you're a Milwaukee Brewers fan, William Contreras needs you to read this
articles.summary: William Contreras: "I'll tell you this: We're a great team. We've been a great team."
articles.body:
Let me tell you something about baseball: No one knows f***ing anything.

Every year, it's the spring, you hear people talk. "The Brewers, I'm thinking they got lucky to win all those games last year ... until the end, and then their luck ran out. They went as far as they can go." OK!!! I mean, I just have to laugh. The playoff series against the Dodgers, we got swept...... It was terrible. I understand why there was not so much belief in us after a loss like that. But if you want the truth, I'll tell you, because I was there. I'm the one who saw it from both sides, right? I'm behind the plate for their side ... and I'm at the plate for our side. Here's the truth: The Dodgers were the lucky team last season.

No, I'm not saying they were lucky to be champions. Of course not. It's a tremendous team, with tremendous players. I'll take nothing away from them. But were they lucky to SWEEP us? That's a different story. Between their team and our team, 4-0, that wasn't the gap. But they made the plays, got the breaks, and by the end of the series we were in our own heads. We're thinking, Those guys........ they found the magic. How else do you explain it??? You can't. After the series, though, a lot of people thought they could explain it. They were like, "That's how it will always go when those teams play..... The Brewers will lose. It's too many stars, too many Hall of Famers, too many great players." People thought that four games told the whole story. And the story to them, it's how we weren't good enough. How we couldn't win the World Series with this group.

But anyone who thinks that way....... to be honest, they don't know baseball. OF COURSE we could win the World Series with this group!!! Come on. Just look at our wins since I've been here: 92, 93, 97, 103. To me, that says a lot about who we are. We're always on top of our division, and always improving. And maybe that's not exciting to some people ... but it's our sport. Grinding and making these little adjustments. Maybe you focus on a few things over the winter. Maybe you sign a few new guys. Maybe a few young guys step up. Maybe you grow a little mentally tougher, a little hungrier. And then you train in the spring, and then you see what you got in the summer, and then you try to capture some magic in the fall. And if it doesn't go your way, then you get back to work in the winter and you do the thing over again. So I'm hearing people bury us after getting swept last season and I'm like, What??? That was four games. That's a short story.

Just ask Pat. He's in the game all his life, it's 65 years until someone gives him a chance to be the man!!! Then he gets his chance and now my guy is the best manager in the league. Or just ask Christian. He's an MVP ... then he deals with these injuries, it's so tough. But nothing tougher than HIM, he sets the standard and that's our captain. Or just ask Jake. Dude is almost gonna retire...... wow. Then he comes back, to help his family out, and now he's letting it rip. Or just ask Brewers fans. The most unbelievable fans. They're so loyal. But a lot of them never seen a World Series game in Milwaukee!!! And they never won it all. It's crazy. Or honestly, man...... even just ask me. 15 years ago? I'm a kid in Puerto Cabello, trying to catch the eyes of some scouts. 10 years ago? I'm a teenager in rookie ball, watching my big bro win his ring with the Cubs. 5 years ago? I'm a backup catcher in Atlanta, working to earn those big league at-bats. And now I'm here.

So it's almost like, to get to THIS moment, we had to have those other moments. Had to take the long way, I swear. And I think the team we are now, how we play fearless, that's where it comes from. We fear nothing, because we've experienced everything. When we got swept like that..... it's disappointment, heartbreak, embarrassment, all those things. So then a year later, Brewers / Dodgers AGAIN, we win the first three but they go up 4-0 in Game 4 ... of course we know what everyone's thinking. About to be Red Sox / Yankees 2004. Dodgers won four in a row last year, they'll do it again. OK. But what are WE thinking? What's the vibe in OUR dugout? I actually won't even say it was calm. It wasn't calm! It was more, Nahhhhh..... LET'S END THIS. So that's what we did.

And just like last year when they swept us, and I said they were lucky to do that, I know this year we were probably lucky to sweep them. I won't sit here and tell you the Brewers are unstoppable. I've been around. I know how quickly things can change in this game. Being hot in your last series, it doesn't mean you stay hot in your next one. But I'll tell you this: We're a great team. We've been a great team. It's just that every year, we've run into a team where it's like, Those guys....... they found the magic. Now it's THE WORLD SERIES though - so I guess it's only two options left??? Either we're about to run into them, or we are them.

articles.title: India script history with best-ever haul of 114 medals as nine golds cap golden day at Asian Para Games
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's para-athletes produced a spectacular finish to their campaign at the Asian Para Games, registering their best-ever medal haul of 114
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's para-athletes produced a spectacular finish to their campaign at the Asian Para Games, registering their best-ever medal haul of 114 medals, including 30 gold, after a record-breaking final-day flourish in Aichi-Nagoya on Friday.India collected nine gold medals on the day — their biggest single-day haul of the ongoing edition — with champions emerging from badminton, archery, shooting and athletics. The country's final tally of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze surpassed its previous best of 108 medals, including 27 gold, achieved at the Hangzhou Games in 2023.The achievement was particularly significant as India competed with a contingent of 168 athletes, nearly half the size of the squad that represented the country in Hangzhou.India remained fourth in the standings at the end of its campaign, although the final positions could change after a few remaining events on Saturday.ALSO READ: Meet India's flag-bearers at closing ceremonyAthletics, badminton lead India's gold rushAthletics remained India's biggest medal contributor, accounting for 65 medals, 12 more than at the previous edition. On Friday, however, the spotlight was shared with a superb badminton campaign and gold-winning performances in shooting and archery.Star javelin thrower Sumit Antil led an Indian 1-2-3 finish in the men's F42-44/61-64 combined event. The reigning Paralympic and world champion threw 72.46m to defend his title, while Mahendra Gurjar took silver with 59.03m and Sandip Sanjay Sargar claimed bronze with 64.48m. Gurjar finished ahead of Sargar on Raza points, which determine rankings in combined-classification events.Pranav Soorma added another gold in the men's club throw F51, defending his title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m. Dharambir secured bronze with 27.71m.Sandeep delivered a world-record performance in the men's 400m T64, clocking 52.28 seconds for gold. India's Ajay Kumar also reached the podium, winning bronze in a Games-record time of 53.61 seconds.Haney produced another world record, throwing 60.49m to win the men's javelin F37/38 title. India also picked up silver medals through Nimisha Chakkungalparambil in the women's long jump T47 and Parmod Bijarnia in the men's 1500m T46, where he clocked 4:09.65.Shuttlers deliver three goldsIndia's badminton contingent delivered three gold medals, led by Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh Kumar and Games debutant Naveen Sivakumar.Nitesh defeated compatriot and Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Pramod Bhagat 21-18, 21-16 in the men's singles SL3 final. He later added a silver medal in mixed doubles SL3-SU5 alongside Thulasimathi Murugesan.Naveen, meanwhile, defeated Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan 21-9, 21-17 to win the men's singles SL4 title.Thulasimathi enjoyed a memorable campaign of her own, combining with Manasi Joshi to win gold in women's doubles SL3-SU5. The Indian pair beat China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in the final.The 24-year-old also secured silver in women's singles SU5 after losing 18-21, 11-21 to Yang in the final, completing a three-medal haul.Mona breaks world record, Harvinder wins archery goldShooter Mona Agarwal added another golden chapter to India's campaign, shattering the world record to win the women's 50m rifle 3 positions SH1 title with a score of 357.5 points.The 38-year-old had earlier won the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 gold with a Games-record score of 250.0 points, edging compatriot Avani Lekhara, who took silver with 249.6.Mona's latest triumph gave her a second gold of the Games and further underlined her standing among India's leading para-shooters. She had also secured India's first 2028 Paralympic quota earlier this year.In archery, Paralympic champion Harvinder Singh teamed up with debutant Vijay Sundi to win the men's recurve doubles gold, defeating China's Yun Duo and Zhao Lixue 5-1 in the final.India's women's recurve doubles pair of Bhawna Choudhary and Pooja Jatyan settled for silver after losing 0-6 to China's Gao Zihan and Wang Xueqian.Swimming contingent exceeds expectationsIndia's swimmers also exceeded expectations, finishing the Games with 11 medals, including three silver.Himanshu Nandal completed a hat-trick of bronze medals by finishing third in the men's 100m freestyle S11. The 22-year-old, who was born blind due to optic nerve failure, clocked 1:05.90, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita (58.22) and China's Chuanzhen Sun (58.70).Nandal had earlier won bronze in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. Ravi Budigina also finished with three medals, comprising two silver and one bronze.With nine gold medals on Friday and a record overall haul of 114, India signed off from its Asian Para Games campaign with its most successful performance at the continental event, surpassing the benchmark set in Hangzhou three years ago.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Kenya’s marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir provisionally banned by AIU
articles.summary: Jepchirchir tested positive for banned blood booster EPO in a sample taken before her Sydney Marathon win in August.
articles.body:
Kenya’s world marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir has been provisionally suspended after testing positive for the banned blood booster EPO in a sample taken before her Sydney Marathon victory , the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) said.

The AIU added that the out-of-competition sample collected in Kenya returned an adverse analytical finding for EPO (erythropoietin), which boosts the production of red blood cells.

“I can only say that I feel terrible about what happened and I think it’s only right that an athlete who uses performance enhancing drugs should be disqualified,” her agent Gianni Demadonna said in an emailed statement.

Sydney Marathon organisers said they were “extremely disappointed” to learn about Jepchirchir’s provisional suspension.

“Jepchirchir is entitled to due process and we will make no further comment on the case until that process has concluded,” organisers said in a statement on social media.

“Our commitment to clean sport is unwavering. Every athlete who lines up in Sydney deserves to race on a level playing field and every participant and spectator deserves to trust the result they see at the finish line.

“That conviction is why, alongside our fellow Abbott World Marathon Majors, we have invested in increased out-of-competition testing in partnership with the AlU, and why we will keep standing firmly with the athletes who compete cleanly.”

The 33-year-old is a former Olympic champion and half-marathon world record holder, as well as a four-time World Marathon Majors winner.

She won gold at the Tokyo Games in 2021 and has also claimed major marathon victories in New York (2021), Boston (2022), London (2024) and Sydney (2026).

Jepchirchir dominated the women’s race in Sydney in August, pulling clear of the field to finish in 2:18:31, more than three minutes ahead of second-placed compatriot Irine Cheptai.

Last year, Kenya’s women’s marathon world record holder Ruth Chepngetich was banned for three years after admitting anti-doping rule violations involving hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ), a prohibited diuretic, though her world record of 2:09:56 remained on the books because it was set before her positive test.

articles.title: Jaime Duro retiene el título mundial en C1 corto
articles.standfirst: En K1 senior corto llegó una nueva medalla para la selección española con la plata de Miriam Vega
articles.summary: En K1 senior corto llegó una nueva medalla para la selección española con la plata de Miriam Vega
articles.body: Jaime Duro logró de nuevo la medalla de oro en la prueba corta de C1 senior de los Mundiales de piragüismo maratón que se disputan en la localidad argentina de Gualeguaychú. Duro, que ya fue campeón el pasado año en Gyor (Hungría), recorrió los 3,40 kilómetros en un tiempo de 12:49.11, con el que superó con claridad al portugués Ricardo Coelho (13:06.10) y al macedonio Serghei Tarnovschi (13:17.82), que completaron el podio. El también español Diego Romero concluyó en la novena posición, a 49.01 de Duro. En C1 senior femenino, María Martín fue sexta a 28:38 de la ganadora, la húngara Borka Zagyvai (15:01.29), que precedió a la ucraniana Liudmyla Babak (15:09.41) y a la rusa Aleksandra Vlasova (15:12.85). En K1 senior corto llegó una nueva medalla para la selección española con la plata de Miriam Vega, que, con un crono de 12:49.35, tan solo fue superada por la sueca Melina Andersson (12:38.45). El bronce fue para la argentina María Garro (12:51.00), en tanto que Eva Barrios concluyó novena con 13:24.12.

articles.title: Marta Bassino: "He aprendido a hablar con mi rodilla, a escucharla"
articles.standfirst: La Copa del Mundo de esquí se abre en Sölden con el regreso de una de sus estrellas después de una año lesionada
articles.summary: La Copa del Mundo de esquí se abre en Sölden con el regreso de una de sus estrellas después de una año lesionada
articles.body: Hace justo un año, Marta Bassino (Cuneo, 27 de febrero de 1996) estaba ingresada en la Madoninna de Milán. A las puertas del estreno de la temporada con el Gigante de Sölden, se había caído entrenándose, en Val Senales. En el quirófano se le redujo la fractura del platillo tibial izquierdo, se procedió a la reinserción del ligamento colateral medial y la sutura del menisco. La temporada saltaba por los aires. No era una más. Porque era la de los Juegos. Sus Juegos. Los de Cortina, en casa. Un año después, está preparada para regresar. Tras meditarlo mucho, hoy estará en el Gigante de Sölden, en el que Italia contará con sus dos estandartes: Fede Brignone y Sofia Goggia. Horas antes de volver a competir, Marta habla con MARCA. Pregunta. Hace ahora un año... Respuesta. Sí. Han sido días un poco extraños, de mezcla de sensaciones. Los recuerdos de la caída, de los días en el hospital... Era inevitable pensar en ello. P. Operada en octubre, en mayo le quitaron la placa. ¿Cómo está la pierna? R. Bien. Todo ha ido bien: la tibia y la rodilla. Estoy contenta de cómo ha ido todo, de cómo ha ido la preparación, de cómo ha ido el mes en Argentina. He aprendido a gestionarlo, a sentirlo. La pierna ha reaccionado muy bien a todo lo que hemos probado y exigido. Me siento bien, me siento estable. Con confianza. P. ¿Mira al pasado y qué ve ese año lesionada? R. Me ha mantenido lejos del mundo de la competición durante todo el año, así que ha sido largo, duro. Pero debo decir que pude aceptarla la lesión de inmediato, aceptar lo que era y concentrarme en mi pierna. Todo lo que me ha tocado vivir, desde la rehabilitación y la fisioterapia hasta recorrer todo el camino para volver a estar bien. P. ¿Qué ha aprendido? R. No sabía que era así, esa parte de Marta. He aprendido a tener mucha paciencia, porque al principio tenía mucho dolor en la pierna y no pude apoyar el pie durante un mes. Dependía de las muletas. Luego, gradualmente, aprender a volver a cargar el peso sobre las piernas. Nunca antes había estado lesionada. Era una afortunada, porque en este deporte... Ha sido todo algo nuevo. Lo que más he aprendido es a tener paciencia, escuchar a la pierna, a hablar mucho con la rodilla. A escucharla, y a los profesionales que me rodeaban: los fisioterapeutas y los preparadores. Todo para recuperar bien la pierna y conseguir que vuelva a realizar todos los movimientos que debe hacer. P. Su lesión coincidió en el tiempo por la recuperación de Fede Brignone. R. Sí. Pasamos mucho tiempo juntas en el J-Medical —centro médico de la Juventus, que trabaja de la mano con la Federación Italiana de Esquí—. Ella estaba en manos de los fisios mientras yo me recuperaba. Estábamos en fases diferentes, porque ella se lesionó en abril y yo en octubre. Fede estaba cerca de volver a esquiar; a mí eso me quedaba lejos. Me dio algún consejo, cómo lo había vivido. Pero cada una es una historia. Lesiones distintas, atletas distintas, caminos distintos... P. ¿Está nerviosa a las puertas del regreso? R. Un poco sí. Hasta este martes no decidí correr en Sölden. Quería tener libertad para elegir si bajaba o no. La verdad, es que Sölden creo que llega siempre un poco pronto. Más este año, después de la lesión. Siento que me falta un poco de todo: entrenamiento, confianza, de lectura de los palos... Pero he decidido correr para volver a sentir las sensaciones de la competición. P. ¿Cómo la afronta? R. Con esa idea de volver a ponerme el dorsal y competir. Sin más idea que recuperar algo que me falta desde la primavera de 2025. P. Sölden son buenos recuerdos para usted. R. ¡Sí! Fue mi primer podio en la Copa del Mundo. ¡Hace justo diez años, madre mía! Y gane en 2020. Me ha regalado recuerdos muy hermosos. Al otro lado está que, para mí, es una de las pistas más difìciles que hay, de las que te da más quebraderos de cabeza, de las más desafiantes. P. ¿Qué le diría la Marta de hoy a la de aquel primer podio? R. ¡Dios mío! Son dos Martas, dos personas totalmente distintas. Hoy soy mucho más consciente de quién soy. Aquella era una Marta de 21 años. Sabía dónde estaba y lo que había conseguido, pero ahora acumulo muchas más vivencias. Me siento distinta gracias a esa experiencia y a todas las cosas que he ido viviendo. P.. Es una temporada con Mundiales. Usted fue oro en el Súper de 2023. Estos son en Crans-Montana, la pista de su última victoria. R.. Eso es, el Descenso de 2024. Pero ahora veo los Mundiales un poco lejos. Es verdad que Crans-Montana es una pista que me gusta, donde logré aquella victoria y fui tercera al día siguiente en el supergigante. Pero vamos a ir paso a paso, carrera a carrera. Siento que todavía me faltan cosas por colocar en su sitio. Después, ya se verá. P. ¿Cómo es la Marta que no vemos? R. Muy sencilla. Me encanta estar en mi casa, en mi tierra. Con mi novio, mi familia, mis amigos. Vuelvo encantada siempre, pero sé lo que exige la vida de atleta. P. ¡Y que no le gusta el frío! R. ¡Padezco el frío! Trato siempre de abrigarme mucho. Me equivoqué de deporte. [Risas]. Es broma, los disfruto mucho. P. ¿Qué otros deportes le gustan? R. Para ver, tenis y atletismo. Con la raqueta hice mis pinitos. Me gusta verlo y jugarlo. P. ¿Tiene algún ritual para concentrarse? R. Tengo mi manera de concentrarme antes de cada carrera. Busco concentrarme sólo en mí misma, aislarme de todo lo que pasa alrededor. Encontrar el equilibrio entre mente y cuerpo. P. ¿Dónde disfruta más compitiendo? R. Cortina. Las pruebas de velocidad en la Olimpia delle Tofane me han gustado siempre mucho. Es muy bonita de esquiar, muy divertida. Para nosotras, las italianas, es un lugar muy especial. P. Entonces tuvo que ser muy duro ver los Juegos desde casa y por la tele. R. Claramente, sí. Pero acepté muy pronto lo que estaba pasando: era una lesión grave, de larga duración, y sabía que no iba a poder estar en los Juegos. Mi cabeza estaba totalmente centrada en recuperar bien la pierna y la rodilla. Claro que sientes cosas, pero la verdad es que los vi bastante tranquila por la televisión. Mikaela Shiffrin: La mejor de todos los tiempos Federica Brignone: Un ejemplo. Sofia Goggia: La fuerza Lindsey Vonn: Perseverancia. Lara Gut: Ídolo. Alice Robinson: Siempre la vi como una joven fortísima. Julia Scheib: Mi esquiadora preferida de la temporada pasada. Emma Aicher: La polivalencia hecha persona. Sara Hector: Una potencia. Es amiga mía. Voy siempre con ella aunque sea una rival. Marta Bassino: Soy yo! ¿A ver qué digo? Determinada.

articles.title: Conte dismisses reports of Man United takeover with Carrick’s job uncertain
articles.summary: Ex-Chelsea boss Antonio Conte denies Manchester United link, says reports he demanded full control of club ‘unfounded’.
articles.body:
Former Chelsea and Napoli coach Antonio Conte said he was not in advanced negotiations to replace Manchester United manager Michael Carrick, and called reports that he had demanded full control at the club “unfounded”.

Conte, who won the Premier League with Chelsea and also managed Tottenham Hotspur in England, was responding to speculation that he had requested full control while also making financial demands of the struggling Old Trafford club.

United sit 13th in the Premier League and 20th in the Champions League standings following Wednesday’s humiliating 4-1 thrashing by Italian side Como, increasing scrutiny on Carrick .

“My name has been linked with numerous clubs, but there are currently no negotiations at an advanced stage,” Conte said in a statement.

“Following a wonderful and successful spell in charge of Napoli, I will take the time I need to consider how and when to return to management,” he added, referring to his time in Naples where he won Serie A in the 2024-25 season.

“It will be a carefully considered decision, one I will make when I believe the conditions are right.

“I have read reports of financial demands and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, as well as reservations about what has been described as my ‘strong personality’.

“These reports are unfounded, as there is currently no concrete basis for such assessments.”

Conte only interest in concrete opportunity with Man United

Conte, who last coached Napoli in the 2025-26 season, said that if a concrete opportunity arose, he would enter talks with the club involved and “jointly consider the terms of a potential agreement”, taking into account the needs of both parties.

“Until then, any assumptions about my demands and my professional future remain speculation and cannot be treated as fact,” the 57-year-old Italian added.

In an interview with The Athletic earlier this month, Conte said he would like to manage a club that has “lost sight of their history” so he can help “make it shine once more”.

Defeat against Como extended United’s winless run to seven games in all competitions, and skipper Bruno Fernandes said his team had adopted a “mood of defeat” while also questioning the tactics, with Carrick apologising for the performance.

Hurzeler ‘focused’ on Brighton job despite Man Utd links

Brighton and Hove Albion manager Fabian Hurzeler, another name linked with the United job, also distanced himself from the speculation on Friday.

The 33-year-old, England’s youngest top-flight manager, said he was focused solely on Brighton, who sit third in the Premier League after a string of impressive performances.

“I have no time to think about these rumours because we play every three days and, beside that, I have a lot of respect for Michael Carrick and what he has done with Manchester United the last season,” Hurzeler told a news conference.

“He’s a great human being, a great personality. There’s nothing more to say about that.”

Brighton’s free-scoring start to the Premier League season has seen Hurzeler touted as a possible successor should United make a mid-season managerial change for the third consecutive campaign.

The Seagulls sit third in the table, behind only Manchester City and champions Arsenal, before Sunday’s trip to Liverpool.

“I am really focused on my job here. I have no time to think about these rumours because we play every three days,” said the 33-year-old German.

Brighton’s scoring streak came to an end in a 0-0 draw at Czech side Jablonec in the Europa League on Thursday.

Despite an excellent start to the campaign, which also includes coming from 2-0 down to beat United 3-2 at Old Trafford in the League Cup last month, Hurzeler believes his side can still improve.

“There is still improvements we can do, still a lot of potential to get out of the players, and therefore I really want to work on that together with my players, together with my staff,” he said.

“I have great experts around me. I have a great group of players who support me, who give everything for this club, and we built this over the last years.

“We had tough periods, we have good periods, but I think to build these kind of relationships, you need time, you need connections, and you don’t take these things for granted.”

articles.title: Connor Hellebuyck Traded to Devils as Jets Suspension Ends, Full Details Revealed
articles.summary: After lobbying for some sort of change following an "unacceptable" season, star goaltender Connor Hellebuyck is getting just that.
articles.body:
After lobbying for some sort of change following an "unacceptable" season, star goaltender Connor Hellebuyck is getting just that.

The New Jersey Devils acquired Hellebuyck from the Winnipeg Jets in exchange for goaltender Nico Daws, forward Dawson Mercer, center Alexander Command, center Nick Bjugstad and two future draft picks.

Quick Predictions on Biggest Storylines 💭

TSN's Darren Dreger , ESPN's Kevin Weekes and The Athletic's Chris Johnston first reported the details.

Johnston and The Athletic's Murat Ates previously reported the suspension the Jets issued to Hellebuyck for failing to report to training camp was expected to expire Friday.

The suspension has cost Hellebuyck $925,000 in forfeited salary, according to Johnston and Ates. The Jets have gotten off to a 4-3-3 start to the season with Stuart Skinner as their go-to starter over that stretch.

Winnipeg is coming off a 2025-26 campaign in which it missed the playoffs and collected the second-fewest points (82) in the Central division.

During his exit interview with the media in April, Hellebuyck was candid when he stated his desire to lift a Stanley Cup and suggested the Jets could need to shake things up.

"From my perspective, complacency is not going to get us moving forward," he told reporters . "So something has got to happen. I'm not going to just sit here and throw every guy under the bus because, honestly, I'm a goalie and I know goaltending really well.

"I can't say, 'Well, this forward did this and that defenceman did that.' That's not my spot. I believe in every guy giving their A-plus effort every single night. As a teammate, I can really rally behind that and really cherish those moments with those guys. But to just put that same product on the ice, I don't think it worked for a reason."

Hellebuyck didn't go so far as to request a trade, but Jets general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff confirmed in June the team was willing to entertain offers.

"Certainly, as an organization we're going to listen," he said. "Everyone saw (Hellebuyck's) press conference at the end of the year; he was passionate. Certainly, in our exit meetings we had some frank conversations as well, but again, what happens in those meetings certainly stays private."

A formal trade request did then arrive in August. Through his agent, Hellebuyck said he approached the Jets months earlier about wanting out but didn't want to publicize it. The lack of movement compelled him to take a different approach.

The situation took another turn when Winnipeg suspended the netminder after he didn't report to camp. Cheveldayoff said he'd be welcomed back when he decided to show up.

Hellebuyck is coming off a down year by his incredibly high standards. His .895 save percentage was a career low, while his 2.86 goals-against average was a notable rise from his NHL-best 2.00 in 2024-25.

Still, the 33-year-old's reputation precedes him. He's a three-time winner of the Vezina Trophy and was the first goalie in a decade to earn the Hart Memorial Trophy in 2024-25.

Thanks to his no-movement clause, Hellebuyck held a lot of the cards in this situation, and his $8.5 million average salary may have priced out some suitors.

There's no ignoring how much of a downgrade the Jets will have between the pipes with Hellebuyck gone.

The Devils, meanwhile, will have a new stalwart between the pipes as they look to return to the playoffs after missing the postseason a year ago.

articles.title: NHL Trade Grades for Connor Hellebuyck to Devils, Dawson Mercer, Picks and Other Players to Jets
articles.summary: The Connor Hellebuyck saga is over in time to avoid a forced, awkward reunion in Winnipeg.
articles.body:
The Connor Hellebuyck saga is over in time to avoid a forced, awkward reunion in Winnipeg.

The Olympic gold medalist gets his wish and heads to an American contender .

The winning team? The New Jersey Devils, who were a reasonable destination to infer, but not one that appeared to be an aggressive pursuer. It's a franchise-altering move for both teams. The Jets move on from arguably the best player in franchise history. The Devils add a real solution in goal for the first time in a decade.

Why did the Devils make this move, given GM Sunny Mehta's skeptical view of goaltending value? Where do the Winnipeg Jets go from here? Let's grade the deal for both teams.

The New Jersey Devils have not had a quality season out of a starting goaltender since Vitek Vanecek in 2022-23, and they have not had a reliable, multi-year option in net since Cory Schneider a decade ago.

Connor Hellebuyck is an affirmative solution to the problem. He's a three-time Vezina winner, and he's led the NHL in goals saved above expected over the last five seasons, per Evolving Hockey. He'll probably end his career as the greatest American goaltender of all time, with 2026 Olympic Gold as the cherry on top.

In previous seasons, the Devils looked like a rising contender being sunk by horrible goaltending. The goaltending has not been awful this season, but both Jake Allen and Nico Daws have been slightly below average. The rest of the team, meanwhile, is playing the skilled, high-octane offense that the team abandoned last season.

GM Sunny Mehta may not see the goaltending position as one generally worth investing in, but he also knows that a player like Hellebuyck is an outlier. Most goaltenders might be great one season and awful the next. Year-to-year data is not nearly as predictive as it is for skaters. But Hellebuyck is one of the five or six who can dependably back a defense over 60-plus starts year-over-year with All-Star numbers.

And as a poker player , he knows when circumstances may signal for him to play a hand he might otherwise stay away from. The market for Hellebuyck was soft, and Winnipeg was reaching both official and optical deadlines for getting this mess off their hands. Now a top-five NHL team by expected goals adds arguably the best goaltender in the NHL (at least, as long as Igor Shesterkin is out).

That doesn't mean the Devils aren't assuming risk. Hellebuyck turns 34 in May and has five seasons remaining at an $8.5 million cap hit . The goaltender position is subject to injury risk, and he has a lot of mileage on his body. Specific to this season, it will not be easy for Hellebuyck to adjust to a new team without any sort of lead-in to the season. Training in a private rink with a few buddies cannot match real practice, let alone live action. How long will it take him to find his form?

Losing Dawson Mercer and Nick Bjugstad also takes a bite out of their bottom-six. Mercer in particular will be missed, though the Devils could afford to part with him. The 24-year-old was forever stuck behind Jack Hughes and Nico Hischier at center and has spent time at wing this season.

Alexander Command is a solid prospect who has second-line upside (though I see him more likely as a third-line center), but the Devils come away with an elite goaltender without giving up an impact player. If Hellebuyck is even just an above-average goaltender in New Jersey the next few seasons, the Devils will shoot into Stanley Cup speculation.

The biggest thing for Winnipeg is that they can now move on.

In whatever way that means. The Jets have been okay to start the season: 11 points in 10 games. The good news is that goaltending has been a pleasant surprise; Stuart Skinner was one of the top goaltenders in October, and Clay Stevenson has held his own as a backup. Their biggest problem has been forward depth. Only the Mark Scheifele and Adam Lowry lines have been able to generate anything. The second line has been awful, and 18-year-old Viggo Björck does not look ready for the NHL, let alone capable of a top-six role.

The Jets are getting a huge infusion of depth with this trade. Dawson Mercer has been flirting with top-six upside his whole career. The 24-year-old was buried behind Hughes and Hischier in New Jersey, which limited his minutes and offensive opportunities. He's been good for roughly 40 points in that role while also playing strong defensively. The Jets should not hesitate to put him on their second line alongside Alex Iafallo and Gabriel Vilardi for what is, in theory, a heavy play-driving line with secondary scoring. Mercer is on a frugal $4 million cap hit and is a restricted free agent in July.

Bjugstad is a veteran fourth-line center who holds down tough defensive minutes. He gives Jets Head Coach Scott Arniel the versatility to move Vlad Namestnikov up the lineup.

Command, taken 12th overall in the 2026 NHL Draft, is a high-floor center prospect. Name an attribute required to play hockey, and he'll grade out as at least adequate in that area. The Swede is a hard-working center who is thorough defensively and in a neutral zone forecheck. The skating is pretty good, and he has a baseline level of puck skill, though it's not consistent. He is likely to be a third-line center in the NHL in a couple of seasons and has upside similar to Mercer's as a middle-six center.

Nico Daws, 25, is a below-average NHL goaltender who has shown moments of upside in spot starts over the last few seasons. He has struggled in four starts (.872 save percentage) this season. Winnipeg now has three goaltenders on the roster, so Daws may be punted somewhere else.

The Winnipeg Jets are trading a franchise goaltender for a quantity of parts. That's not a winning trade on the merits. Of course, the Jets are only making this trade because they had no choice. Hellebuyck wanted out. One has to trust that this was the best offer on the table. Given that Hellebuyck was a sunk asset for this season anyway, the Jets at least come away a stronger team for this season and add pieces in Mercer and Command who could make an impact long-term.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson reveals high ankle sprain, remains uncertain for Bengals
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson revealed he has a high ankle sprain and said his movement will help determine whether he can return against Cincinnati
articles.body:
Lamar Jackson is recovering from a high ankle sprain, and the Ravens quarterback says his ability to move effectively will help determine whether he returns against Cincinnati on Sunday. Jackson identified the injury Friday after missing Baltimore's past two games. He said the swelling has decreased but stopped short of committing to the Bengals matchup.

"Right now, I'm heading in the right direction," Jackson said, according to Jamison Hensley.

Jackson described the sprain as painful and said playing without his usual movement would do his team a disservice, according to Jeff Zrebiec. The comments provide additional context for an injury that forced Jackson out at halftime against Tennessee on Oct. 4. He was listed as limited Wednesday and Thursday before returning to the field for Friday's practice.

Jackson's mobility is a significant part of Baltimore's offense. Through four appearances, he has rushed for 144 yards and a touchdown on 19 carries, averaging 7.6 yards per attempt. He has also completed 70.8% of his passes for 967 yards, six touchdowns, and one interception, for a 119.6 passer rating.

Tyler Huntley is 1-1 in his two starts, helping Baltimore win in overtime in Atlanta before Sunday's 13-10 loss to Cleveland. Huntley completed 19 of 31 passes for 165 yards and a touchdown against the Browns.

Jackson's practice progress is encouraging, but his assessment makes clear that returning requires more than getting on the field. Baltimore needs him to execute the movement and improvisation that make its offense difficult to defend.

articles.title: Rockets' Kevin Durant eyes challenging matchups with Spurs
articles.summary: The future Hall of Famer pointed to the defending Western Conference champion's versatility and depth, and, of course, Victor Wembanyama.
articles.body:
AUSTIN - Future Hall of Famer Kevin Durant pointed to the Spurs' versatility and depth, and, of course, superstar Victor Wembanyama, when asked about the long-term matchup between the Houston Rockets and their Interstate 10 rivals.

"They're reigning Western Conference champions for a reason," Durant said before the teams squared off Friday night in the first of four meetings between the clubs this season.

"They're a deep team. They got one of the most unique players that ever touched the floor at the center position (in Wembanyama). And then they got plenty more guys on their team that can wreak havoc. They got a 6-foot-6 point guard, Dylan Harper, and (All-Star guard) De'Aaron Fox. They just got a line up of guys that can do pretty much a lot of things on the floor. And then they're playing fast-paced basketball shooting threes: The new modern era basketball mixed with a 7-5, 7-6 guy (Wembanyama) who (can shoot from distance).

"So it's going to be tough. We got our work cut out for us, but that's an amazing part about the NBA season. You get thrown into these tests early on and we're looking forward to it."

The Spurs, likewise, believe they will have their hands full defending Durant after watching him pump in 30 points in helping the Rockets coast to a 128-110 victory over the Dallas Mavericks on Wednesday night in the season opener for both teams.

"As he showed in game one, still flying high," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said of Durant. "He hasn't slowed down and it's a testament to the work he's put in and his preparation, all he's done in the offseason for a lot of years now. And it's a joy to watch."

The Spurs and the Rockets don't meet again until Jan. 26 when they square off at the Frost Bank Center in a game set for national television on NBC.

The final two meetings between the teams will be in Houston on March 5 and March 16.

Friday night's game marked the second time Durant has faced the Spurs in Austin, where he starred for Texas as a freshman in 2006-2007 before the Seattle SuperSonics made him the the No. 2 overall pick in the 2007 NBA Draft.

Durant scored 22 points with the Phoenix Suns in a 120-109 loss to the Spurs on Feb. 20, 2025 at the Moody Center.

"It was just a perfect partnership," Durant, 38, said of his time with the Longhorns. "Even though it was a short amount of time, I think the impact I had here in that one year was felt for a while. And then the impact that this community had on my life has been felt for the rest of my life. This is like my foundation. The day I graduated high school, the next day I came to Texas by myself. I was here for that whole year. No friends, no family. I had to meet everybody here.

"So I grew up, learned a lot about myself, learned some legendary coaching with coach (Rick) Barnes and his staff in a great city I had no clue about until I got here. So everything worked out perfect."

articles.title: Lakers vs. Clippers: What to watch in second game of season
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES — The Los Angeles Lakers established an early connection around the basket in their season opener.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES — The Los Angeles Lakers established an early connection around the basket in their season opener. Their next opponent found plenty of success inside, too.

After beating the Golden State Warriors 127-105 on Wednesday, the Lakers host the Clippers on Friday at Crypto.com Arena, with both teams looking to build on convincing opening-night victories.

Luka Dončić, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler combined for 77 points in the Lakers' win. Now, L.A. could get its first look at another offseason addition as Collin Sexton prepares to join the rotation.

Here are three things to watch in the Lakers' second game of the season.

Both teams made scoring inside a significant part of their opening-night wins.

The Lakers scored 66 points in the paint against Golden State, with Kessler contributing 26 points and nine rebounds. The Clippers scored 56 paint points in their 121-96 victory over Sacramento.

Friday presents an opportunity to see which team can maintain that production while making the other work harder around the basket.

For the Lakers, that starts with Dončić and Reaves creating openings through their drives and work with Kessler. His screens and rolls can force defenders to choose between stopping the ball and staying close enough to prevent a finish.

Defensively, L.A. must limit penetration without surrendering easy passing opportunities behind the help. Kessler's presence matters, this is a huge test to see what he can bring inside mucking up any shot attempt, but the guards and wings must also need to keep the Clippers from repeatedly reaching him with an advantage.

Sexton is available after being removed from the injury report, putting him in position to make his Lakers debut following a right soleus strain.

His arrival gives JJ Redick another option to initiate the offense and attack the basket when Dončić or Reaves rests.

The first thing to watch is how Sexton balances his own scoring opportunities with getting teammates involved. His speed can help create early offense, but also rust can be a factor in his play with not playing a single minute in the preseason.

Jake LaRavia's questionable status with a right ankle sprain adds another variable as Redick assembles his bench groups.

Garland scored 30 points in the Clippers' season-opening win, making him an immediate focus for the Lakers' perimeter defense.

Containing him begins with the Lakers wings in Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams getting the start next to Dončić, Reaves and Kessler.

Thybulle had the assignment on Stephen Curry in the opener, so look for him to take on the Garland assignment for this matchup as well.

articles.title: Browns’ Todd Monken reveals bold Deshaun Watson ceiling bet that could push Shedeur Sanders out
articles.summary: Todd Monken explains why the Browns bet on Deshaun Watson’s ceiling over Shedeur Sanders, and what it means as trade buzz builds.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken chose Deshaun Watson over Shedeur Sanders by chasing ceiling, and six games into the 2026 season, the offense looks like that wager.

Speaking on Ryan Clark's podcast "The Pivot," Monken said his staff measured both quarterbacks by their peak snaps. Sanders produced highlights of his own, he said, "but we just saw a little bit more from Deshaun at the top end."

"I think you try to look at what a player's best is and then try to minimize the weaknesses," Monken said.

That logic explains both halves of Cleveland's 4-2 start. Watson has now led four drives that put the Browns ahead late in games, precisely the peak plays Monken was buying. The floor surfaced against Baltimore, when Cleveland gained 46 net yards and punted on five straight possessions before halftime, then edged the Ravens 13-10 to grab first place in the AFC North.

Monken settled on Watson on Aug. 24 after weighing offseason workouts, training camp, a joint session with Buffalo and two exhibition games. Sanders finished last season as the starter and went 3-4 in seven games.

Watson was coming off two Achilles surgeries, carrying a $230 million guaranteed contract and facing fans still angry over the se*ual as*ault accusations, his league suspension and the draft capital Cleveland spent to land him.

Shedeur Sanders' Trade Market Hinges on the Same Peak-Play Test

In Monken's telling, one of Watson's biggest moments came before a snap. Ahead of the Week 4 game against Pittsburgh, the Browns introduced him last out of the tunnel, and a crowd that had booed him roared instead.

"They want good football. They want our players to play well," Monken said.

Cleveland beat the Steelers 27-24 after a scoring march in the final stretch flipped the lead.

Against Baltimore, Watson found Jerry Jeudy for 33 yards on a 10-play, 62-yard possession that ended with Andre Szmyt's game-winning field goal. Monken pinned the slow starts on himself and his offensive staff while backing his quarterback's instincts.

"But he's just got something in him, the ability to make a play when needed," he said. "We're always under construction."

The ceiling standard also frames what comes next for Sanders. He hired an agent earlier this month, a move widely read as a step toward leaving, with the trade deadline under three weeks away.

Yet the evaluation that kept him on the bench is the same one rival front offices would run, and Sanders has had no chance this season to display the progress he made in camp. With little outside demand so far, a deal won't come easily. Monken's offense gets its next chance to raise its floor Sunday at Tennessee, where the 1-5 Titans are waiting.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown Calls Out Ex-Celtics Teammate Jayson Tatum Over Comments on 76ers Trade
articles.summary: Tatum and Brown were teammates for nine seasons
articles.body:
Sixers' Jaylen Brown called out his former teammate Jayson Tatum in a comment on social media

Brown posted a "cap" emoji on an interview Tatum did sharing his recount of learning Brown was being traded to Philadelphia in July

Tatum said he was "just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world" when the news of Brown's trade was announced

Jaylen Brown called out his former teammate Jayson Tatum 's recollection of learning the Celtics traded Brown to Philadelphia.

In a video shared to his YouTube on Thursday, Oct. 22, Tatum, 28, shared his recount of the moment he learned the Boston Celtics had traded his longtime teammate to the Philadelphia 76ers in July. Tatum said he was in Las Vegas at the time, and recalled ESPN insider Shams Charania breaking the news to him.

"I just got done playing pickup the first day. Shams walks over, he hands me the towel, he's like 'Yo, put this over your face, don't react, they just traded him," Tatum said.

The Celtics star shared that he asked Charania where the Celtics sent Brown, and when he learned it was Philadelphia — where Brown would team up with LeBron James — he recalled thinking they "traded him down the street."

Tatum said he was "just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world" after his teammate was traded, but it appears that Brown doesn't entirely believe Tatum's recount.

In the comments of a clip of Tatum's interview, Brown, 29, reacted with an emoji of a baseball cap, which in internet lingo means you're calling "cap" on someone and accusing them of lying.

Brown and Tatum shared the court in Boston for nine seasons. The Celtics finalized their trade with the Sixers on July 6, sending Brown to Philadelphia in exchange for Paul George, a 2028 first-round pick, a 2031 first-round pick, a 2028 second-round pick, and a 2030 second-round pick.

The duo led the Celtics to the 2024 NBA championship, and Brown was named the Finals MVP.

articles.title: Brazil in Libertadores and Copa Sul-Americana finals for sixth year running
articles.summary: Palmeiras and Atlético-MG represent Brazilian football in the CONMEBOL Libertadores and CONMEBOL Sudamericana finals, respectivelyCredits: Cesar Greco/Palmei...
articles.body:
Palmeiras and Atlético-MG represent Brazilian football in the CONMEBOL Libertadores and CONMEBOL Sudamericana finals, respectively Credits: Cesar Greco/Palmeiras and Pedro Souza/Atlético

For the sixth consecutive year, Brazilian football will have representatives in the finals of the CONMEBOL Libertadores and CONMEBOL Sudamericana, South America's premier club competitions. In the Libertadores final, Palmeiras will face Estudiantes, while Atlético-MG will take on Boca Juniors in the Sudamericana.

In the Libertadores, Brazilian dominance is even greater. Since 2019, teams from the country have won every edition. In 2020 (Palmeiras vs. Santos), 2021 (Palmeiras vs. Flamengo), 2022 (Flamengo vs. Athletico-PR), 2024 (Botafogo vs. Atlético-MG) and 2025 (Flamengo vs. Palmeiras), the finals were all-Brazilian affairs. In 2019, Flamengo defeated Argentina's River Plate, and in 2023, Fluminense beat fellow Argentine side Boca Juniors.

During this period, Palmeiras won the title in 2020 and 2021. Having also been crowned champions in 1999, they are chasing a fourth title and will face Argentina's Estudiantes, winners in 1968, 1969, 1970 and 2009, who beat Flamengo on penalties this Thursday (22).

To reach the final, the Alviverde defeated Fluminense, also on penalties, on Wednesday (21). The CONMEBOL Libertadores final will take place on November 28 at the Estadio Centenario in Montevideo, Uruguay.

Brazil has had representatives in the CONMEBOL Sudamericana final for six seasons. Over that period, only Athletico-PR, in 2021, lifted the trophy, beating Red Bull Bragantino. Since then, São Paulo (2022), Fortaleza (2023), Cruzeiro (2024) and Atlético-MG themselves (2025) have finished as runners-up.

This year, Galo have the chance to win their first title in the competition and bring the Sudamericana trophy back to Brazilian football. In the semifinals, they eliminated Uruguay's Montevideo City Torque on Wednesday (21) and will face Boca Juniors in the final, after the Argentine side knocked out Vasco on Tuesday (20).

The final will take place on the 21st of next month at the Estadio Metropolitano Barranquilla in Barranquilla, Colombia.

articles.title: Pac-12 Power Rankings Heading Into Week 8
articles.summary: The race for the Pac-12 championship is starting to take shape as we head into Week 8. Boise State and Oregon State remain the teams to beat, while San Diego...
articles.body:
The race for the Pac-12 championship is starting to take shape as we head into Week 8. Boise State and Oregon State remain the teams to beat, while San Diego State is gaining ground after a big win over Fresno State. With several teams still looking to establish themselves, this week's matchups could help us establish the true top half of the conference.

The Broncos have occupied the No. 1 spot in the power rankings all season, and that does not change with Boise State coming off a bye week.

Boise State will look to keep its College Football Playoff run alive with a game against Washington State, which appears to have turned a corner offensively with a new quarterback under center. The Broncos will need to establish the run and limit defensive mistakes to beat the Cougs in Pullman.

I feel like a broken record, but it's another week and another impressive offensive performance from the Beavers. Washington State's defense has been solid this season, but Oregon State was able to pick it apart and score more than 40 points in a dominant performance.

Questions remain about the Beavers' defense after allowing 31 points to a WSU offense that has struggled to move the ball and put points on the board this season. Oregon State will have a bye week to make some defensive adjustments before a big Halloween matchup against Fresno State.

Coming into their rivalry week matchup, Fresno State was regarded as the clear third-best team in the Pac-12. San Diego State changed that perception with a 26-23 win over the Bulldogs, moving to 2-1 in Pac-12 play. The victory gives the Aztecs a legitimate shot to establish themselves as a top-three team and compete for a spot in the Pac-12 championship game.

Week 8 brings a Colorado State team that has struggled to get stops on defense all season. The Aztecs should feel good about their chances to improve to 3-1 in Pac-12 play before facing WSU in Week 9.

The Bulldogs appeared to have established themselves among the top three teams in the conference and as a legitimate threat to Boise State and Oregon State in the race for the Pac-12 title. While they are not out of the race yet, those hopes took a significant hit with a loss to San Diego State.

The Bulldogs head into their bye week at 1-2 in conference play before a must-win game against Oregon State next week. If Fresno State falls to 1-3 in Pac-12 play, it would spell disaster for a team that entered the season with its sights set on a conference championship.

The explosive Texas State offense was too much for a struggling Colorado State defense. The Bobcats overpowered the Rams 66-27 to pick up their first-ever Pac-12 conference win. Texas State's offense is one of the best in the conference and gives the Bobcats a chance to win every game.

Texas State has a chance to improve to 2-1 in Pac-12 play this week with a home game against Utah State. The Aggies have struggled to put points on the board all season. If Texas State can score 30 or more points again this week, the Bobcats should feel good about their chances.

The Aggies move up a spot during their bye week thanks to another embarrassing performance by the Colorado State defense.

Coming off the bye, Utah State will travel to Texas State for a matchup against an explosive Bobcats offense. The Aggies' defense will need to come up with plenty of stops to keep the game competitive, especially with an offense that has struggled to put points on the board this season.

An offense that was dormant for seemingly the entire season finally woke up in Week 7 against Oregon State. WSU started a new quarterback, Owen Eshelman, and he appeared to have better command of the offense.

Looking ahead, WSU faces another top Pac-12 team in Boise State this week in Pullman. The offense will need to build on its success in Corvallis if the Cougars want to pull off an upset against a ranked Boise State team this weekend.

The Rams drop to the bottom spot in this week's rankings after allowing more than 50 points for the third consecutive week. Jim Mora still has some serious issues to address on defense if Colorado State wants to win another game this season.

This week provides as good an opportunity as any for the defense to get back on track with a matchup against San Diego State. If the Rams can make strides defensively and get some stops, their offense is good enough to beat the Aztecs.

articles.title: Liverpool not helping Andoni Iraola; €60m transfer plan is a mistake
articles.summary: Liverpool aren't helping Andoni Iraola with their latest transfer plan. The €60m idea is a mistake.Liverpool are building their transfer shortlist for the up...
articles.body:
Liverpool aren't helping Andoni Iraola with their latest transfer plan. The €60m idea is a mistake.

Liverpool are building their transfer shortlist for the upcoming windows and there's certainly work to be done. Richard Hughes left Julian Ward with a very imbalanced squad and one with holes all over the place.

On top of that, there are upcoming holes - contracts that need sorting or this group will be decimated by inaction. It's a difficult spot for Ward, then, especially as he needs to sign players pretty quickly.

One area of concern is midfield. Liverpool have built a group entirely of attacking midfielders and while the opportunity was there in the summer to sign someone different, the Reds instead sold Curtis Jones and signed no one.

It was a bizarre move - but we worry Liverpool could double-down on it.

TuttoMercatoWeb reports that Liverpool remain in the mix for Manu Koné. The AS Roma star was the subject of interest by many clubs in the summer, and the report claims that Chelsea mad a €60m offer.

That offer was rejected and Roma expect a bigger one to arrive from someone in 2027. The Reds and the Blues are the only clubs named as definitely interested in the Frenchman.

But we're not sure about this one. Koné is a very good player but not one proven to be truly elite. That wouldn't usually be a problem - you can always develop a player to that level - but he's incredibly close to what Liverpool already have.

Our Value Adder model has Koné as very similar going forward as Ryan Gravenberch. In fact, that's the most similar player to him across the top five leagues in attack.

This isn't something that helps Iraola. More of the same isn't the order of the day - the problem isn't squad depth or a need for cover. The issue is that Liverpool don't have controlling, defence-first midfielders who can stop counter-attacks and plug gaps.

Koné would be more of the same, essentially a swap-out for Gravenberch in games. Liverpool would largely be in the same position they're in right now, which isn't worth €60m.

articles.title: Kon Knueppel & Coby White Injury Update: Why The Hornets May Be In Huge Trouble
articles.summary: The Charlotte Hornets opened their season with a road win, beating the Brooklyn Nets 110-103. Charlotte heads to Spectrum Center tonight to take on the Atlan...
articles.body:
The Charlotte Hornets opened their season with a road win, beating the Brooklyn Nets 110-103. Charlotte heads to Spectrum Center tonight to take on the Atlanta Hawks, but two starters have already been ruled out: Kon Knueppel and Coby White .

Previously, the Hornets stated they would re-evaluate during the first week of the regular season. That time is now, and both players are still out. How concerned should Hornets fans be that Knueppel and White are still out due to injury?

Kon Knueppel's Injury Is Extremely Impactful — But Not Alarming

Both Knueppel and White sustained injuries during training camp and missed every preseason game. Knueppel has a left hamstring strain, and White has a left calf strain. Soft tissue injuries are always a nuisance in any sport, and Charlotte has kept them out of games out of an abundance of caution.

The Hornets were able to squeak by with a win to open the season on Wednesday without Knueppel. Grayson Allen poured in 21 points on an extremely efficient 6-for-9 from the field (5-for-8 from three), showcasing his Sixth Man of the Year potential.

Brandon Miller , Naz Reid , Moussa Diabate , and Dennis Schroder all scored 17 or more points. Head Coach Charles Lee's team got it done that night, but can they expect the same performance against a stronger team like the Atlanta Hawks?

The Hornets attempted 48 three-pointers against the Nets, accounting for 51.6 percent of all their shots. They only converted 31 percent of those 48 three-pointers, a brutal reminder of how Knueppel's efficient shooting helps this offense so much. The turnovers were still relatively high at 20, which was one of the biggest Hornets storylines in the preseason.

Knueppel's hamstring strain is not expected to be long-term. Since the Hornets never officially announced the grade of the strain, it should be assumed to be grade 1 (mild), which carries a shorter recovery timeline.

The Hornets are taking a cautious approach with their young star. When the franchise views you as a cornerstone in the post- LaMelo Ball era, it is okay to take it slow to begin the year. Knueppel also doesn't have an extensive injury history.

His next chance to play would be Saturday vs. the Miami Heat. Expect Knueppel to return at some point before the October slate ends.

Coby White's Recurring Calf Injury Is Very Concerning

On the other hand, White's calf strain is worrisome. It was definitely an upgrade when the Hornets traded for White with multiple second-round picks and Collin Sexton , but availability is the best ability.

If Charlotte fans remember, when the Hornets originally acquired White, he was sidelined for a few weeks with a similar calf injury. The left calf injury during training camp is either a recurring injury or a setback from the original one.

White has had repeated calf injuries throughout his career, but the one silver lining is that he's been able to play 60+ games in every season with the exception of last year. The question remains: will this be an occasional flare-up for the rest of his career?

When the Hornets traded the injury-plagued Ball, they signed White to a long-term deal to be their starting point guard. The hope is that he doesn't end up having an injury-plagued career in Charlotte and repeat history all over again.

The Hornets are going to proceed with caution and ensure both of these players are fully healthy before they get on the court. It's the best decision, but it leaves the Hornets at a moderate disadvantage.

Even if Knueppel's injury isn't too worrisome and he returns in the next week, the Hornets could possibly be without White for a longer timetable since he has a longer injury history of repeated calf issues.

If that happens, then it's the Schroder/ Christian Anderson Jr. show until further notice — a bleak outlook considering the Hornets' grueling schedule in the upgraded Eastern Conference.

articles.title: FHSAA to announce football playoff bracket, Open Division at 5 p.m. Nov. 6

articles.body:
The FHSAA announced that its football bracket release show will be on Friday, Nov. 6 at 5 p.m.

The FHSAA will announce who's in, who's out, and playoff seedings for multiple different postseason tournaments - most notably the State Championship series and the new Open Division .

The State Championship series is the traditional championship playoffs with Classes 1A-6A. Each class will have 32 teams in a bracket for their respective state championships.

The Open Division will pull the top-8 ranked teams in the state , regardless of class, to compete for one title. The eight teams will enter pool play, then the top two teams from each pool will face off in a single elimination tournament.

Last year's bracket release show featured a bit of drama, and the stage is set for more fireworks this year. A judge signed an order to temporarily lift a postseason ban on The First Academy just two hours before the show began, forcing the FHSAA to delay revealing the Class 1A bracket until the issue was settled in court.

This year, Carol City was handed a postseason ban after a postgame fight in Grayson (Ga.) , and submitted their appeal at the buzzer. The Chiefs are currently ranked No. 6 in MaxPreps' Florida rankings, meaning they would qualify for the Open Division. How Carol City's appeal goes through would directly impact the Open Division, and if they slip out of the top-8, would have major implications on Class 2A's playoff picture.

The FHSAA's bracket reveal will be live on their YouTube channel .

Uncertainty continues to hover above Lamar Jackson entering a big divisional matchup versus the Cincinnati Bengals , but the Baltimore Ravens superstar quarterback is at least making progress in his recovery from an ankle injury. How gradual is it, though?

Following back-to-back limited practices, Jackson was on the field again on Friday. He did not do much jogging or running during the portion that was open to the media, however, according to ESPN's Jamison Hensley. Although Jackson's presence is encouraging, his participation obviously does not guarantee an "active" designation for Sunday's face-off with Cincy.

The Ravens have to balance their pursuit of AFC North supremacy with their franchise keystone's long-term health. Jackson himself wields some influence over the decision and can potentially give the green light. He cannot just will himself back to full mobility, though.

Baltimore must decide if it can properly protect the two-time MVP from further injury, otherwise this squad will find itself in survival mode yet again. If he is on the gridiron, fans should be in for a treat.

Jackson and Joe Burrow have contested some memorable battles over the years, and the former usually prevails. The Bengals have a new-look defense, however. They rank tied for sixth in the NFL with 17 sacks (in five games), with huge offseason acquisition Dexter Lawrence accounting for three of them. Baltimore's offensive line better be ready.

But will Lamar Jackson be? The Ravens will ideally update his status by day's end. Tyler Huntley will make his third consecutive start if No. 8 is forced to miss another game.

articles.summary: Racing Bulls driver Liam Lawson took to the stage for a rare live music performance in Austin ahead of the United States Grand Prix
articles.body:
Liam Lawson had some familiar faces in the crowd as he took to the stage in Austin on Thursday night.

The New Zealander headlined Garage Sessions with Liam Lawson and Friends at part of Esses Bazaar ATX, held at Inn Cahoots on East Sixth Street ahead of this weekend's United States Grand Prix.

Daniel Ricciardo , who Lawson replaced at Racing Bulls in 2024, was there to watch along with current team-mate Arvid Lindblad and former team-mate Isack Hadjar .

Lawson performed alongside his brother Marcus and two childhood friends, Thomas and Harrison, in what was his first public performance since he was 11.

"I am feeling a lot of things. I mean, I'm excited for... It's a cool opportunity to do this with my brother and a couple of friends that I've grown up playing with," the 24-year-old told the media in Austin ahead of the performance.

"To be honest, we haven't done this for like 10 years. And obviously, we never really performed, but we grew up playing together when we were very young. So it's a cool opportunity. But no, I'm sh***ing myself, for sure."

articles.title: Ravens rule out Jaylinn Hawkins with knee injury ahead of Bengals
articles.summary: Jaylinn Hawkins has been ruled out against Cincinnati with a knee injury. Jesse Minter indicated the issue is not expected to be long term
articles.body:
The Ravens will face Cincinnati's passing attack without safety Jaylinn Hawkins, who has been ruled out for Sunday's game with a knee injury.

Coach Jesse Minter indicated Friday that the injury is not expected to be a long-term issue but did not provide a specific return timetable, according to Brian Wacker. Hawkins has appeared in all six games this season, making three starts and recording 30 tackles, including 17 solo stops. He matched his season high with eight tackles in Sunday's 13-10 loss at Cleveland.

His absence requires another adjustment for a secondary preparing to defend Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Cincinnati arrives after its bye, while Baltimore tries to recover from its first division loss.

Kyle Hamilton and Malaki Starks remain central to the Ravens' safety options. How Baltimore replaces Hawkins' snaps could also influence Hamilton's deployment, given his responsibilities near the line of scrimmage and in coverage.

Hamilton has played 33% of his snaps in the slot, 33% at linebacker and 20% at safety, according to Next Gen Stats figures cited by Cincinnati's official scouting report. That versatility gives Baltimore flexibility, but replacing Hawkins still requires balancing its coverage and run-defense assignments.

The Ravens also learned Friday that outside linebacker Tavius Robinson will miss the remainder of the season with a pectoral injury.

Hawkins' outlook appears less severe, but his immediate absence leaves Baltimore replacing contributors at two levels of its defense against a rested division rival.
