articles.title: Winners and Losers of the Connor Hellebuyck to the Devils Trade
articles.summary: The Connor Hellebuyck saga is officially over.
articles.body:
The Connor Hellebuyck saga is officially over.

The Jets traded the 33-year-old three-time Vezina winner to the Devils Friday in exchange for forwards Dawson Mercer, Alexander Command and Nick Bjugstad, goalie Nico Daws, a 2029 second-round pick and a 2027 seventh-round pick.

Hellebuyck is in the third year of a seven-year contract carrying an $8.5 million AAV. He requested a trade during the offseason, and the team placed him on an unpaid suspension for sitting out training camp. He missed all of training camp and the first 24 days of the regular season, forfeiting $927,835.05 in salary .

There were offers on the table from contenders like the Hurricanes and the Sabres, but the Jets took their time and landed on the package from the Devils as Hellebuyck's unpaid suspension expired Friday.

Winnipeg never had much leverage to play around with, here, but how did they do now that all is said and done? Will Hellebuyck's new home give him a better opportunity to achieve success in the playoffs?

Here are the winners and losers of Hellebuyck to the Devils.

The Devils have been trending in the right direction after a rougher start to the season, but they've still got work to do as they sit at fourth in the brutal Metropolitan Division with a 6-4-0 record.

Production hasn't been the problem, as Jack Hughes is averaging more than a point per game and depth scoring has been solid, but goaltending has been an issue since trading Jacob Markström. Jake Allen and Nico Daws have been splitting the net, and both have put up mediocre-to-bad performances. Allen's got a 3.15 GAA and an .883 save percentage through six games, while Daws has a 2.78 GAA and an .876 save percentage through four games.

Who better to come in and round out this group than Hellebuyck?

To top it all off, the Devils didn't have to give up any key players or a first-round pick. Mercer has been a solid defense-first forward for the Devils, but he appears to have hit his ceiling offensively. The haul they sent over was hefty in volume, but not in true impact on the team.

The Devils and GM Sunny Mehta clearly win this round of poker.

The Jets were going to be losers in this deal from the moment Hellebuyck requested a trade. All things considered, though, they still fumbled the little leverage they had in the situation.

Yes, Hellebuyck is a 33-year-old goalie; yes, he's coming off of a down season; and yes, he had a pesky no-movement clause. Still, he's a three-time Vezina winner and a Hart Trophy winner. He is more often than not the best goaltender in the NHL, and he's particularly hungry for some playoff success.

The Jets did not get a first-round pick or any remotely on-par player in a deal where they shipped off the most elite player at the most coveted position in the league. The Senators got three first-round picks and a second-rounder for Brady Tkachuk.

We also know that the Jets turned down several offers before landing on this one, and both the Sabres and the Hurricanes reportedly had competitive offers on the table. It's tough to stomach that a team struggling so much offensively didn't get an enticing scorer or the hope of drafting one in this deal.

Losers: NHL Teams That Still Need Goaltending

The Hurricanes and the Sabres were two teams heavily in the Hellebuyck mix for a reason: Both are seeking either elevated or more consistent goaltending to contend for a Cup.

The Hurricanes are doing fine, leading the NHL with 18 points to start the season after letting Freddie Andersen leave via free agency to the Oilers, but underlying stats indicate that goaltending could regress. According to MoneyPuck.com , Pyotr Kochetkov is ranked 19th league-wide with 2.3 goals saved above expected through six games, and despite his undefeated record, he's got a .899 save percentage. Brandon Bussi is off to a rough start, averaging more than three goals allowed per game, with a 2-2 record and a .865 save percentage.

Meanwhile, the Sabres are in an even more dire situation. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen is struggling with -3.7 goals saved above expected, an .864 save percentage, and a 3.53 GAA through eight games. As the Sabres sit at the bottom of the Atlantic, they could really use the best goaltender in the game to turn things around.

Quick Predictions on Biggest Storylines 💭

Winner: The Sweepstakes for Quinn Hughes

The Hellebuyck trade is the first of many dominoes to fall that could very likely end up impacting Quinn Hughes' future .

It's no secret that Hughes, set to become a free agent at the end of this season, is eyeing the opportunity to play with his brothers in New Jersey. He's made it clear, though, that as lovely as that would be, his number one priority is winning.

You know who he won Olympic Gold with last season? Oh yeah, Connor Hellebuyck. You know who elite defensemen value? Elite goaltenders.

Hellebuyck to New Jersey could end up creating a butterfly effect for the Hughes situation with several create-your-own-adventures. The Devils could climb to the top of the Metro and entice Hughes at the deadline or in the offseason.

On the other hand, maybe Wild GM Bill Guerin is watching this play out and thinking, "How can we do everything in our power to keep Hughes in Minnesota?"

Winner: The Sweepstakes for Dylan Larkin

Speaking of Guerin doing everything he can to keep Hughes in Minnesota, the Hellebuyck trade is coming days after the news tha t Larkin expanded his trade list to 10 teams . Things were already heating up in the Larkin sweepstakes, and they're expected to come to a head shortly.

The Wild were on Larkin's short list of three teams from the start, and they remain on his expanded list. The Wild also need another elite center to tie the bow on a near-perfect roster. Perhaps acquiring Larkin would convince Hughes to extend with the Wild and contend for a Stanley Cup, and perhaps Hellebuyck to New Jersey puts the necessary pressure on Guerin to get it done.

Beyond Hughes and the Wild, the Hurricanes are always looking to improve, and GM Eric Tulsky cannot resist a good contract. After losing out on the Hellebuyck sweepstakes, could the Canes throw their hat in the ring for Larkin?

articles.title: WWE Rumors on Rey Mysterio's Retirement, Roman Reigns, Oba Femi, CM Punk, Cody Rhodes & Nikki Bella
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Rey Mysterio Reportedly May Be Mulling 2027 Retirement

Way-Too-Early WrestleMania 43 Predictions 🔮

Ranking Wrestling's Hottest Storylines 🔥

Changes WWE Needs for WrestleMania 43 🛠️

WWE Hall of Famer Rey Mysterio reportedly could be set to wrestle the final match of his illustrious career in 2027.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News), there have been "rumblings" within WWE regarding Mysterio possibly retiring next year.

WWE has reportedly "discussed ideas on how to present," although it isn't yet known when or where his retirement match would take place, or who it would be against.

The 51-year-old Mysterio has long been regarded as one of the luchadores of all time, as well as one of the greatest professional wrestlers in general.

He has been an active wrestler since 1989, and he continues to perform at a high level even today, as evidenced his the Triple Threat match between him, Chad Gable and Dragon Lee this week on Raw.

Mysterio earned a rare honor in 2023 when WWE inducted him into the Hall of Fame despite still being an active wrestler.

While Mysterio has shown no real signs of slowing down, retirement has to come eventually, and it would be fitting if it happens in 2027 given that fellow legends John Cena and AJ Styles retired within the past year as well.

Mysterio is the on-screen general manager in AAA, and even if he retires, he could continue to serve in that role while also contributing behind the scenes.

On top of that, Rey's son Dominik is a top star on Raw and his daughter Aalyah is training at the WWE Performance Center, so there is plenty of incentive for him to remain involved with the company even in retirement.

Latest on Reported Reigns vs. Femi, Punk vs. Rhodes WrestleMania Plans

A recent report regarding WWE's planned main events for WrestleMania 43 may not have been entirely accurate.

Last week, WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t WrestlePurists ) reported that WWE was discussing Roman Reigns vs. Oba Femi and CM Punk vs. Cody Rhodes for WrestleMania this coming April.

However, Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer Newsletter (h/t WrestlePurists ) followed up Friday by reporting that while Reigns vs. Femi is indeed in the plans, Punk vs. Rhodes is not.

Reigns vs. Femi being the direction for WrestleMania 43 is no surprise given that the groundwork was made back at WrestleMania 42.

After Femi defeated Brock Lesnar and Reigns beat Punk for the World Heavyweight Championship, Oba called out Roman during the post show.

Then, following Femi's win over Bronson Reed and Reigns' win over LA Knight at Money in the Bank, Oba spoke about his desire to challenge The OTC once again.

As for Punk and Rhodes, they already met in a WWE Championship match at SummerSlam, which Punk won.

They left enough meat on the proverbial bone to go back to it, but the WWE Championship scene on SmackDown is crowded with plenty of big stars in the mix.

Sami Zayn is the reigning champ, but Punk, Rhodes, Randy Orton, Kevin Owens, Finn Balor and Gunther are just a few of the Superstars vying for an opportunity.

Punk vs. Rhodes at WrestleMania 43 very much feels possible, but with so many moving parts, it is far from guaranteed.

WWE Reportedly Considering Major Nikki Bella Push

WWE has reportedly been impressed with Hall of Famer Nikki Bella as of late, and she could potentially be in line for a significant push.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Mukherjee ), Bella has been "drawing praise" within WWE recently, and the company has taken particular notice of her strong numbers on social media.

Bella has reportedly "exceeded expectations" with her social media impact and merchandise sales, and a source indicated that they would not be surprised if Nikki is given a "bigger spotlight" moving forward.

A two-time Divas champion, Bella returned to WWE in 2025 as a surprise entrant in the women's Royal Rumble match, and she has been back wrestling on a semi-regular basis since June 2025.

While an injury kept her off the WrestleMania 42 card, Nikki returned in July and turned heel by attacking Paige.

Nikki and Paige have been embroiled in a rivalry ever since, and they have traded wins and losses on SmackDown.

At the same time, Bella has had several backstage segments with WWE women's champion Chelsea Green in recent weeks, which could be foreshadowing an eventual match between them.

Should that happen, perhaps Nikki has a chance to become the new women's champion more than a decade after she last held the Divas Championship.

articles.title: European Championship: Luke Littler through as Michael van Gerwen makes early exit
articles.summary: World champion Luke Littler makes it through to the second round of the European Championship with a win over William O'Connor but Michael van Gerwen is knocked out of the tournament at the first-round stage.
articles.body:
World champion Luke Littler made it through to the second round of the European Championship with victory over William O'Connor - but Michael van Gerwen was knocked out at the first-round stage.

Teenager Littler hit six 180s and had a three-dart average of 105 in his 6-3 victory in the best-of-11 contest - his first match since a surprise semi-final defeat at the World Youth Championship in early October.

The world number one will next play Nathan Aspinall, who beat Cristo Reyes 6-3, in Dortmund as he tries to complete the set of major trophies by winning the European Championship.

"Obviously, [I've played] a few exhibitions, but yeah, just obviously been chilling out, practicing, and this is the one I really want," said Littler, 19.

"I've just got to take it one game at a time, and obviously it's the last one missing, so I can't be putting too much pressure on myself.

"I'm just happy to get back on stage and do my job."

Van Gerwen, 37, was up against fellow Dutchman Kevin Doets and, after going 5-1 down, the three-time world champion was comprehensively beaten 6-3.

The 28-year-old Doets will face Krzysztof Ratajski, who beat Dave Chisnall 6-2, in the last 16.

Jonny Clayton and Josh Rock will take on each other after their respective 6-3 and 6-1 wins against Niko Springer and Chris Dobey.

German Martin Schindler came through a deciding leg as he beat Wessel Nijman 6-5 to set up a match against Jermaine Wattimena, who was a 6-3 winner against England's Ryan Joyce.

Humphries withdraws from European Championship

articles.title: European Championship Darts: Luke Littler sets up Nathan Aspinall clash as Michael van Gerwen is dumped out in Dortmund
articles.summary: Luke Littler opened his Machineseeker European Championship title bid with a dazzling victory over William O’Connor on Friday, as debutant Kevin Doets dumped out Michael van Gerwen in round one
articles.body:
Littler is in Dortmund, trying to win the only big event he has yet to claim in a dominant first two years on the scene.

He got off to a good start on Friday night with a 6-3 win over O'Connor, with six 180s to set up a second-round clash with Nathan Aspinall.

The teenager is set to take part in a huge Netflix show next week where 24 players are vying to win £501,000 by beating him in a one-off leg, and asked whether his focus is on this tournament, he said: "This is the next one after the World Youths, so I knew how much time I would have off.

"Obviously, (I've played) a few exhibitions, but yeah, just obviously been chilling out, practicing, and this is the one I really want."

The 19-year-old has not played since a surprise defeat in the World Youth Championship and has enjoyed the break.

"I think I'm more focused because of the amount of time we've had off," he added. "I mean, I have not been doing too much, but I've been practising.

"I've just got to take it one game at a time, and obviously it's the last one missing, so I can't be putting too much pressure on myself.

"I'm just happy to get back on stage and do my job."

Littler also revealed he had changed his grip and throw during a lengthy recent lay-off from competitive action to stave off a feeling of boredom in practice.

"I think it's just having so much time off. I had loads of weeks to prepare for this, so I can just go to the practice board at home and just kind of change it, really," he said.

"I hit a nine-darter the other night on DartCounter as well, so I was like... 'I think I will stay with this until something does go wrong'. But it is all going well so far."

After Luke Humphries withdrew with illness, Littler's possible path to glory looks even easier as Michael van Gerwen crashed out on Friday night.

Van Gerwen is not the player of old and went out 6-3 to Dutch compatriot Kevin Doets .

"It was a tough game," assessed Doets, who will take on Krzysztof Ratajski on Saturday evening.

"The draw comes out and I get Michael… it's still Michael van Gerwen. He is the one I looked up to for years and the most successful player from the Netherlands.

"He didn't play like he can, but I'm really happy to win. I felt through the whole game that I was the better player.

Ryan Joyce also had a day to forget as he suffered a 6-3 defeat to Jermaine Wattimena .

Joyce travelled from the North East on Friday morning, but his luggage did not make it to Dortmund.

He had to borrow some darts from a local collector, who had a similar set to the one he uses.

But he found himself 5-0 down and faced darts for a whitewash before putting up a brief fightback.

Aspinall set up his tie with Littler after reeling off four straight legs to see off Cristo Reyes, including finishes of 134, 112 and 90 to come back from behind.

There were also wins for Josh Rock and Martin Schindler .

The European Championship continues with a crucial double session on Saturday, as all 16 remaining players return for round two.

Defending champion Gian van Veen takes on Luke Woodhouse in the pick of the afternoon ties, while Littler and Aspinall lock horns in the evening session.

articles.title: Northern Ireland Open: Kyren Wilson and Mark Williams through to NI Open semi-finals
articles.summary: Former Northern Ireland Open champions Mark Williams and Kyren Wilson win through to the semi-finals of this year's tournament in Belfast.
articles.body:
Former Northern Ireland Open champions Kyren Wilson and Mark Williams remain on course for a potential meeting in the final of this year's tournament in Belfast after winning their respective quarter-finals on Friday.

World number nine Wilson ran out a convincing 6-1 winner over Anthony McGill in the afternoon session at the Waterfront Hall, while Williams, who sits one place higher in the rankings, defeated David Gilbert 6-4 during the evening's play.

Wilson, who claimed both the world title and the NI Open crown in 2024, established a 4-0 lead over his Scottish opponent with the help of breaks of 77, 75 and 122.

McGill took the next with a run of 66 but the Englishman eased home to progress and secure a first semi-final appearance at a ranking event since March 2025, with compatriot Sam Craigie his next opponent.

Craigie advanced to only his second-ever ranking event semi-final by beating Elliot Slessor 6-2.

Slessor took an early lead after compiling an 82 but Craigie reeled off five frames in a row and ultimately clinched a comfortable passage to the last four.

Gilbert built a 3-1 lead over Williams with the help of breaks of 62, 95 and 60, but after they shared the next two, Williams scored three centuries in consecutive frames as he took the next four to seal victory.

The 51-year-old three-time world champion and 2017 NI Open winner will take on fellow Welshman Jak Jones in Saturday's second semi-final.

Jones, who has already collected the British Open and Championship League titles this season, edged out Scott Donaldson 6-5 in a late-night thriller, a break of 84 in the decider proving decisive in booking his berth in the last four.

articles.title: Tennessee Titans vs. Cleveland Browns: 5 players to start/sit for fantasy football in Week 7
articles.summary: Here's a look at some start/sit decisions for fantasy football in the Week 7 matchup between the Tennessee Titans and Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans will look to build on their Week 6 victory when they host the Cleveland Browns on Sunday, and fantasy football managers will have some difficult lineup decisions to make ahead of the matchup.

Tennessee is coming off a 26-20 comeback victory over the Indianapolis Colts , while Cleveland enters the contest following a 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens . With both teams coming off defensive battles, fantasy managers will need to be selective when setting their lineups.

There are a few intriguing opportunities in this matchup, particularly in the backfield, but not every player should be trusted this week.

Here are five players to start or sit in fantasy football for the Titans' Week 7 matchup against the Browns.

The second-year quarterback has shown flashes of potential throughout his first season, but his inconsistent production has made him a difficult option to trust in fantasy lineups.

Ward completed 11 of 22 passes for 102 yards against Indianapolis in Week 6, struggling to generate much through the air before Tennessee mounted its comeback.

Unfortunately for Ward, the matchup against Cleveland doesn't offer much relief. The Browns have one of the more disruptive defensive fronts in the league, and their ability to pressure opposing quarterbacks could create problems for Tennessee's passing game.

Ward's rushing ability provides some added fantasy appeal, but his limited passing production and turnover risk make him difficult to trust outside of deeper superflex formats.

Sit: Deshaun Watson, QB, Cleveland Browns

Although Cleveland has managed to win games, Watson's fantasy outlook remains underwhelming heading into Sunday's matchup.

The veteran quarterback has struggled to consistently generate explosive plays, and Tennessee's defense could make things difficult with its ability to pressure the pocket and force opponents into uncomfortable situations.

The Titans are coming off a strong defensive performance against Indianapolis, recording six sacks and forcing three turnovers. That type of production should give Tennessee confidence heading into this matchup.

Watson's rushing ability can provide some additional fantasy value, but his inconsistency as a passer makes him a risky option in standard leagues.

Unless fantasy managers are dealing with significant bye-week or injury problems, Watson is best left on the bench.

Start: Quinshon Judkins, RB, Cleveland Browns

Judkins has emerged as an important piece of Cleveland's offense, and his workload makes him an attractive option for fantasy managers heading into Week 7.

His ability to contribute as both a runner and receiver gives him multiple paths to fantasy production, even if Cleveland struggles to establish its passing game.

That could prove particularly valuable against a Tennessee defense that has shown improvement recently but still needs to prove it can consistently contain opposing backfields.

Judkins' volume should be his biggest selling point. If Cleveland can keep the game competitive and establish its rushing attack, he has the opportunity to deliver a productive afternoon.

With his health no longer a major concern, Judkins is a start as an RB2, with additional upside if he finds the end zone.

Start: Carnell Tate, WR, Tennessee Titans

The rookie wide receiver has shown the ability to create separation and make plays downfield, giving him an opportunity to become a reliable contributor in the Titans' offense.

Tate's biggest obstacle has been the inconsistency of the passing attack. Ward's struggles have limited the upside of Tennessee's receivers, making it difficult for fantasy managers to confidently project their weekly production.

However, Tate's target share and involvement in the offense give him an appealing path to fantasy relevance.

The Browns' defense presents a difficult matchup, and fantasy managers shouldn't necessarily expect a massive performance. Still, Tate's ability to make plays on limited opportunities makes him an intriguing flex option, especially in deeper leagues.

He's a start for managers looking for upside, although expectations should remain tempered.

Start: Tony Pollard, RB, Tennessee Titans

Pollard is the Titans player fantasy managers should feel most comfortable starting this week.

The veteran running back remains a key component of Tennessee's offense, and his workload gives him a reliable opportunity to produce even in a difficult matchup.

Pollard has averaged 17.4 touches and 67.8 total yards per game since Week 2, making him a consistent source of volume despite some disappointing fantasy finishes.

The matchup against Cleveland won't be easy. The Browns have the defensive personnel to make running lanes difficult to find, and Tennessee's offensive struggles could limit scoring opportunities.

However, Pollard's involvement in the passing game gives him a potential avenue to fantasy production if the Titans fall behind or struggle to move the ball on the ground.

He's a reasonable RB2 for Week 7, with touchdown potential providing additional upside.

articles.title: UTSA to wear helmet decal to honor fallen airman
articles.summary: UTSA will wear a commemorative helmet decal in remembrance of the airman who died after falling during a pregame demonstration.
articles.body:
The UTSA football team will wear a commemorative helmet decal in remembrance of the airman who died after falling during a pregame demonstration on Saturday at the Alamodome.

The decal, which bears Air Force Technical Sergeant Ian Patterson's nickname, "Patty," will also be worn by the rest of the teams in the American Conference during this week's games.

Moments of silence will be observed ahead of UTSA's road football game against Tulane at 7 p.m. Saturday in New Orleans, as well as at UTSA's home volleyball match against UAB on Friday and home soccer match against Temple on Sunday.

Patterson fell Saturday during a rappelling demonstration at the annual Salute to Armed Forces and Veterans football game between UTSA and Navy. He later died at an area hospital. The Air Force has not released details about what led to Patterson's fall.

The Spurs also honored the U.S. airman game with a moment of silence just before the playing of the national anthem in the team's home opener at the Frost Bank Center on Tuesday.

A decorated airman from Fort Stewart, Ga., Patterson was a tactical air control instructor in Detachment 2 of the 6th Combat Training Squadron, assigned to Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland.

Patterson received a number of decorations during his 15 years of service, including the 2022 Air Force Special Warfare Enlisted Instructor of the Year award at the Headquarters Air Force level. He also received the Air and Space Commendation Medal with three oak leaf clusters, the Army Commendation Medal with one oak leaf cluster, the Air and Space Achievement Medal with one oak leaf cluster and the Army Achievement Medal with one oak leaf cluster.

articles.title: Kevin Harvick Reacts To Christopher Bell’s Admission About Kyle Larson
articles.summary: Kevin Harvick agreed with Christopher Bell that Bell and Kyle Larson are not friends. Harvick said there is respect between them and compared it to his own r...
articles.body:
Kevin Harvick says Christopher Bell and Kyle Larson are both right about not being friends. The two drivers are first and second in the NASCAR Chase standings. Harvick reacted on his Happy Hour podcast.

Bell and Larson were asked about their relationship during a joint media session at Phoenix Raceway on Saturday.

"I think it's fair to say that we're different people, and we hang out with different people, and we're not friends, but we're acquaintances, and we've raced each other hard," Bell said.

Larson agreed and said Bell has pushed him to improve.

"I think nobody's pushed me more than Christopher to become a better racer, so I appreciate that," Larson said.

Harvick said the rivalry is fun to watch.

"There's a rivalry there that we all enjoy watching when it happens, and they're able to race against each other because they're both extremely talented and in extremely good equipment," Harvick said.

"And they're both right. It has made them better. And they know that they're not the same people. They don't like to do the same things," Harvick said.

"They aren't friends. I believe that there's a lot of respect there for one another. It's just that they don't like losing to the other one," Harvick said.

Harvick compared it to his own rivalry with the late Kyle Busch . Both ran their own Truck Series teams while racing against each other in the Cup Series.

"I think that Kyle Busch made me better. We competed head-to-head with the Truck Series teams with everything that we had on that side," Harvick said.

"And sometimes on those weekends, by the time we got to Sunday, we had probably run into each other a few times at some point because of the competitiveness between the two of us and our organizations for so many years," Harvick said.

The 2014 Cup champion said his only close friend among drivers was Tony Stewart . He explained why those friendships are rare at the top level of motorsports .

"Having those relationships that are close throughout the years… You're there to race for your team and do the best that you can for your team and worry about the consequences later," Harvick said.

"It's tough because sometimes you gotta run your friends over," Harvick added.

Bell is five points behind Larson with three races left. They race Sunday at Talladega Superspeedway.

articles.title: Navarrete and Foster In Three-Belt Shootout in San Antonio Saturday
articles.summary: What to Know Three belts will be on the line in a sensational super featherweight unification fight shootout in San Antonio between Emanuel Navarrete and O’S...
articles.body:
Three belts will be on the line in a sensational super featherweight unification fight shootout in San Antonio between Emanuel Navarrete and O'Shaquie Foster on Saturday.

In the co-feature, undefeated prospect Albert "Chop Chop" Gonzalez will take on two-time world title challenger Edward Vazquez

The fight card airs on DAZN Boxing with the main card at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT. Before the bell action starts at 5:30 p.m. ET/2:30 p.m. PT on DAZN, Top Rank and DAZN's YouTube channels, and the Top Rank Classics FAST channel on Roku, Tubi, Pluto and Vizio.

If you believe boxing is all about the best fighting the best, Saturday night's card from San Antonio is what you've been waiting for.

Two exciting world champions will put themselves to the test against a tough style matchup between a boxer and a puncher. WBO and IBF World Super Featherweight champion Emanuel Navarrete (40-2-1, 33 KOs) will face WBC World Super Featherweight champion O'Shaquie Foster of Houston, Texas (25-3, 12 KOs).

All fighters made weight Friday, although Navarrete initially came over four-tenths of a pound and had to get on the scale twice to hit the 130-pound limit. Foster weighed in at 129.8 pounds.

"I feel great, man. I'm ready to rock out. We got one more day," said Foster after stepping down from the scale. "Y'all know what it is. It's shock the world, man," promising Navarrete would run into "a lot of punches" and he would dominate every round.

It's a brave statement given the track record of his opponent. "Tomorrow is a big day where we're all going to find out who's the best at 135," said Navarrete, cheered on by the San Antonio fans. "So I'm happy and I'm grateful for all the support for the people here … I'm going to deliver a great fight."

How does El Vaquero plan to get past the Foster defense? "I have to try to hit him a lot. I need to pressure him a lot in order to win," said Navarrete, who admitted he can't obligate Foster to engage, but he would do his work and bring the titles back home."

Too often, fight card titles are uninspired. Top Rank got it right, calling the Navarrete vs Foster matchup "Fire and Ice."

Navarrete is the fire, an offensive machine with a nonstop engine. With an 82% knockout rate, he's never in a boring fight. What separates Navarrete from many other classic "Mexican Style" offensive punchers is his unorthodox approach using unusual angles and awkward footwork. Often, he appears off balance or out of position. But somehow, Navarrete makes it work for him in a way no one else can copy.

Navarrete generates a high punch output behind relentless, never-ending pressure that he's able to deliver due to his conditioning. He's not a one-hitter quitter type puncher. Instead, he wears his opponents down and they give out in the later rounds.

Navarrete has struggled in performances when he struggles to make weight, such as his single loss to Denis Berinchyk and his narrow escape from Charly Suarez. Navarrete worked with a nutritionist for his last fight against the highly regarded Eduardo "Sugar" Núñez . After 42 fights, Navarrete never looked better. He's in the best possible position to add another belt to his collection.

"We corrected certain things and worked differently, from nutrition to the type of preparation. I also had to make some adjustments personally. But the most important part is that we really concentrated and stuck to the game plan, and I think the result will be resounding," said Navarrete this week.

Navarrete also said he knows the fans don't want to see a defensive fight with nothing but jabs, and he doesn't want that either. "They want to see a war. They want to see both fighters come in intending to win the titles. I'm talking about an attractive fight, a tough fight, maybe even a bloody fight."

If anyone can disarm this version of Navarrete, it is the savvy ring general who stays cool under fire: O'Shaquie Foster, the ice in this matchup.

Foster said this week it's a fight he's been chasing since he signed with Top Rank three years ago, the fight he's always wanted.

It took Foster a little time early in his career to put his skills together. He's learned to read the room and remain patient, using his high ring IQ to dictate his approach. He never rushes into a fight. He gets a feel for its rhythm, tricking his opponents to committing to punches and evading them with his superior footwork. He looks for openings and uses a snapping, stiff jab and crisp counterpunches.

Foster has more than enough power to hurt his opponents. He makes aggressive punchers like Navarrete uncomfortable, and they often push hard to get to Foster. He capitalizes on their mistakes, uses his defensive skills, and brings out the firepower. He has been compared to Terence Crawford for his blend of offense and defense, and his adaptability in the ring.

"We got him in the position we want him, and we just got to seal the deal Saturday," said Foster. "I'm ice water, man. I flow with it. I'm cool, calm, collected. I don't fight to other people's advantages. Whatever he brings to the table, I'll adjust, and it's going to be a great night.

Foster said Navarrete talks a good game, but he doesn't like getting hit. "He'll trade with you, but we'll see. If he does that, it'll be a great night for me. I'm not going to lie to you."

If Navarrete comes out hot, Foster will work on cooling him down. If he can successfully freeze out Navarrete, he can win the fight. But when Navarrete comes into the fight in top condition as he did against Nunez, he should be able to put the pressure on Foster and outlast the slick tactics to come out the winner.

Chop Chop Gonzalez Steps Into the Spotlight

In the 10-round featherweight co-feature, unbeaten Albert "Chop Chop" Gonzalez of Riverside, California (18-0, 11 KOs) steps up against Fort Worth native and former two-time world title challenger Edward Vazquez of Fort Worth, Texas (20-3, 6 KOs) . Boxing fans are starting to find out what Southern Californians have known about Gonzalez. He's an exciting young talent and exactly what boxing needs.

Trained by Robert Garcia, Gonzalez will get the kind of serious test he needs against Vazquez. Other than getting sparked out by Rafael Espinoza, Vazquez put up solid efforts in losses against Joe Cordina and Raymond Ford. If Gonzalez can join Divino Espinoza as the only other opponent to stop Vazquez, he jumps to the top of our list as a possible Prospect of the Year.

Super lightweight contender Frank Martin of Indianapolis (19-1-1, 13 KOs) looks to jump-start his boxing career against Tarik Zaina of Morocco (18-3-1, 12 KOs) in a ten-round fight. Martin's only loss came to Gervonta Davis at lightweight. He struggled to save a draw against Nahir Albright in his first fight at super lightweight. We'll see what Martin has to offer in this test.

Scooter Davis and Joaquin Faccio Step Up

Moving up from the before the bell card to open the main show, lightweights Deric "Scooter" Davis of Fort Washington, Maryland (12-0, 10 KOs) and Joaquin Faccio of Uruguay (10-1, 4 KOs) get a golden opportunity to impress fans and build their case for bigger matchups in an eight round bout.

Bantamweight Steven Navarro of Los Angeles came two pounds over the weight limit Friday, His fight with his former amateur rival Emanuel Moreno of Wichita Falls, Texas is now off.

articles.title: Diamond volleyball advances in Class 2 District 11 tourney
articles.summary: DIAMOND — The sixth-seeded Diamond High School Wildcats volleyball team (8-21-4) advanced to the semifinals of their Class 2 District 11 tourney with a 3-0 (...
articles.body:
DIAMOND — The sixth-seeded Diamond High School Wildcats volleyball team (8-21-4) advanced to the semifinals of their Class 2 District 11 tourney with a 3-0 (25-16, 25-14, 25-15) win over the third-seeded Sarcoxie High School Bears (13-17-2) on Thursday night at Diamond High School.

Backed by a large rowdy crowd of supporters, the Wildcats gained an early 8-1 advantage that included an ace by Addy Ellis and a Lilly Hoyer kill from the left wing.

Sarcoxie battled back with a 5-point run, but after an Aubrey Curtis kill and two Ainsley Webb service aces, the Wildcats were on top 11-6. Diamond later extended its lead to 13-7 off a kill in the middle by Codi Sweet.

The Bears managed to claw back within 2 points at 13-14, but Diamond put together 3 points in a row to go up 17-13.

Up 17-14, the Wildcats scored 7 straight to increase their lead to 24-14. After giving up a pair of points to Sarcoxie, Callie Thomas closed out the 25-16 Set 1 win for Diamond with a kill in the middle.

The Bears claimed the early lead in the second set, going up 7-3. Diamond erased that deficit after a timeout that saw the Wildcats return to the floor and put together a 13-0 run. That 13-point stretch was sparked by an Ellis kill and was capped off by a Thomas ace that gave Diamond a 16-7 lead.

Up 18-11, the Wildcats put together another run, this one 6 points, that gave them a 24-11 lead. Sarcoxie tallied the next 3 points to make it 24-14, but Webb closed out the Set 2 win with a kill in the middle.

The teams played close in the early stages of the final set, until Diamond, up 12-9, went on a 7 point scoring spree that included another Ellis kill. The Bears got 4 of those points back to close within 5 at 19-14, but Diamond scored the next 5 points on a run that included a Curtis block.

Sweet later closed out the 25-15 win with a block in the middle that sealed the Wildcats 3-0 match win.

Diamond head coach Chad Adams assessed his team's play after the win.

"They came out ready to play," Adams said. "Offensively, we really had a lot of energy and defensively, we stepped it up. We haven't played good defense all season, but we really stepped it up tonight.""

With the win, Diamond advances to face second-seeded Miller High School (19-11-2) in the semifinals at 7 p.m. Monday. The team's met on Oct. 6 with the Cardinals logging a 3-0 (25-19, 25-16, 25-8) win.

Adams is well aware of what his team is up against on Monday. He talked about how to prepare for a strong Miller squad.

"We'll watch a lot of film and talk about where the holes are at," Adams said. "We know what they did to us last time and where they scored on us. I think, offensively, we can pay against them. Defensively, we came up short last time. I think this time we will be ready and at least make it a closer game."
authors: Laurie Sisk, The Joplin Globe, Mo.

articles.title: Wilson and Williams through to NI Open semi-finals
articles.summary: Former Northern Ireland Open champions Mark Williams and Kyren Wilson win through to the semi-finals of this year's tournament in Belfast.
articles.body:
Former Northern Ireland Open champions Kyren Wilson and Mark Williams remain on course for a potential meeting in the final of this year's tournament in Belfast after winning their respective quarter-finals on Friday.

World number nine Wilson ran out a convincing 6-1 winner over Anthony McGill in the afternoon session at the Waterfront Hall, while Williams, who sits one place higher in the rankings, defeated David Gilbert 6-4 during the evening's play.

Wilson, who claimed both the world title and the NI Open crown in 2024, established a 4-0 lead over his Scottish opponent with the help of breaks of 77, 75 and 122.

McGill took the next with a run of 66 but the Englishman eased home to progress and secure a first semi-final appearance at a ranking event since March 2025, with compatriot Sam Craigie his next opponent.

Craigie advanced to only his second-ever ranking event semi-final by beating Elliot Slessor 6-2.

Slessor took an early lead after compiling an 82 but Craigie reeled off five frames in a row and ultimately clinched a comfortable passage to the last four.

Gilbert built a 3-1 lead over Williams with the help of breaks of 62, 95 and 60, but after they shared the next two, Williams scored three centuries in consecutive frames as he took the next four to seal victory.

The 51-year-old three-time world champion and 2017 NI Open winner will take on fellow Welshman Jak Jones in Saturday's second semi-final.

Jones, who has already collected the British Open and Championship League titles this season, edged out Scott Donaldson 6-5 in a late-night thriller, a break of 84 in the decider proving decisive in booking his berth in the last four.

articles.title: Liam Lawson welcomes special guest Daniel Ricciardo to Austin concert
articles.summary: Daniel Ricciardo made an appearance at a special event organised by Liam Lawson in Austin ahead of the United States Grand Prix. The former Formula 1 driver...
articles.body:
Daniel Ricciardo made an appearance at a special event organised by Liam Lawson in Austin ahead of the United States Grand Prix. The former Formula 1 driver was among several familiar faces who attended the New Zealander's first live musical performance.

Lawson swapped his racing duties for a guitar on Thursday evening, taking to the stage at an event called Garage Sessions with Liam Lawson and Friends. The Racing Bulls driver performed alongside his brother Marcus and two childhood friends, with the group putting on an acoustic music session ahead of the race weekend at the Circuit of the Americas.

The event took place at Inn Cahoots in Austin and also marked the launch of Lawson's partnership with Taylor Guitars. The New Zealander performed with a customised LL30 GS Mini Special Edition guitar, featuring his racing number and a cartoon design also found on his helmet.

Lawson's interest in music dates back to his childhood, with his father playing in a band and encouraging both him and his brother to learn the guitar from the age of six. The Racing Bulls driver has continued playing throughout his Formula 1 career, regularly sharing videos and photographs of himself with his guitar on social media.

Speaking ahead of the event, Lawson explained the personal significance of performing alongside his brother and childhood friends: "I feel very proud to be launching my partnership with Taylor Guitars at Garage Sessions."

"Playing the guitar has been a big part of my life since I was young, as my Dad played in a band throughout my childhood. He encouraged my brother and me to play since we were six years old, so it feels like a full-circle moment to be launching a custom LL30 GS Mini SE while performing with my brother and two friends who I grew up playing with."

The New Zealander also explained how music helps him switch off from the demands of Formula 1: "Music is a big part of my life, and I use it to clear my head during the season, so I'm really excited to perform at Garage Sessions where we can connect with fans outside of the track. I'm looking forward to meeting everyone there."

Ricciardo joins familiar F1 faces at Lawson's concert

Ricciardo was among the guests attending the performance, alongside Lawson's current Racing Bulls team-mate Arvid Lindblad and former team-mate Isack Hadjar, who now races for Red Bull.

Several country music artists were also present, including Alison Nichols, Jonathon Capeci, Scoot Teasley, Jess Farren and Drake Milligan, who headlined the F1 Grid Gig in Austin last year.

Racing Bulls shared a photograph of Lawson and Ricciardo on social media on Friday, showing the two drivers together before the New Zealander took to the stage. The team accompanied the picture with the caption: "Nothing like seeing a familiar face before hitting the stage."

The occasion also brought together two drivers whose Formula 1 careers crossed paths in 2024. Ricciardo made his final Grand Prix appearance for Racing Bulls at Singapore that year, before Lawson replaced the Australian for the remainder of the season.

The eight-time Grand Prix winner returned to Austin ahead of this weekend's United States Grand Prix, where Lawson will resume his racing commitments with Racing Bulls.

articles.title: Christian Horner admits he may never return to F1 after Red Bull exit
articles.summary: Former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner has revealed he is in no rush to return to Formula 1
articles.body:
Christian Horner has explained that he is in no hurry to return to Formula 1 and that he could live with never working in the paddock again.

Horner was sacked as Red Bull Racing CEO and team principal in July 2025, ending 20 years in charge. Speaking to CBS News anchor Errol Barnett at the Autosport Business Exchange in New York on Wednesday, he said any comeback would have to be a serious project.

Autosport Business Exchange returned to New York City for its second edition, bringing together senior leaders from across motorsport, business and brands at the Manhattan Motorcars showroom to examine racing's growth in AmericaChristian Horner made his first U.S. appearance at the event since leaving Oracle Red Bull RacingOther panellists included seven-time NASCAR Cup Series champion Jimmie Johnson, former chairman and CEO of Formula 1 Chase Carey, General Motors' Mark Reuss, Penske's Jonathan Gibson and NASCAR's Tim Clark

"To be honest with you, I'm not in any particular rush," Horner explained. "And I'm happy just sitting on the periphery at the moment, just watching, having experienced life outside of Formula 1 the last 15 months and knowing the sacrifices that it takes to win in Formula 1.

"For me to go back, it would have to be for the right project. The sacrifices that you need to make, the amount of time it is away, the hours it dominates your life. It would have to be with like-minded people who wanted to win.

"I've won almost a third of the races that I've ever entered in Formula 1, and I wouldn't want to go back just to take part. I'd want to go back to compete and then be in a position to invoke change. So it'd have to be something pretty compelling to convince me to go."

Horner has released his autobiography, Drive . When asked if the book hinted at a potential return to the paddock, the Briton explained he would be satisfied with what he has achieved already if his time in the championship is done.

"Honestly, I have no idea. I've loved my time that I've done in the sport. I'm a fan of the sport. I'm a fan of Formula 1," he explained.

"And for me, if that's my time done in Formula 1, I'm OK with that. I'm proud of what I did, and I feel privileged to work with who I did, but there's still a competitive desire within me.

"And if the right opportunity presented itself, under the right conditions, then I would be prepared to go back, but it would have to be with people who wanted to win at the end of the day. I wouldn't want to go back just to take part. That just has no appeal to me."

articles.title: NHL Rumours: Montreal Canadiens Changing Trade Strategy
articles.summary: The Montreal Canadiens have consistently been in NHL rumours since leading up to the NHL trade deadline for the 2025-26 season. General Manager Kent Hughes h...
articles.body:
The Montreal Canadiens have consistently been in NHL rumours since leading up to the NHL trade deadline for the 2025-26 season. General Manager Kent Hughes has been rumoured to be aggressively seeking a top-notch top-six forward to play alongside star forward Ivan Demidov . But the latest in NHL rumours is that the Canadiens are changing their trade strategy. Let's get into the details.

NHL Rumours: Montreal Canadiens Changing Trade Strategy

Rumour: In a Thursday article for Sportsnet , Hockey Insider Frank Seravalli provided some inside information as to how the Canadiens are approaching the trade market. He said that "the start of the season from some of their young players has the Canadiens internally weighing how aggressive they want to be on the trade market." He said Montreal's "big move" this season may be more along the lines of the deal they made for Phillip Danault last season, to add a stabilizing player that doesn't cost much in future assets and does not have long-term strings attached.

Analysis: The Seravalli article does not address the injury to Nick Suzuki and was likely written before the injury was announced. But the injury may strengthen Seravalli's assertion. If Hughes was reluctant to part with young assets before, the price will only go up with potential trade partners knowing how badly the Canadiens will miss Suzuki. Hughes is more likely to seek out a lower-cost stabilizing option, if any deal is made at all while the captain is sidelined.

Recapping Recent NHL Rumours for the Canadiens

Montreal has been connected to several prominent players on the trade market. Leading up to last season's deadline, they were trying to strike a deal with the Toronto Maple Leafs for Matthew Knies . Throughout the offseason, they pursued Kirill Marchenko from the Columbus Blue Jackets. Most recently, they have been connected to Dylan Larkin of the Detroit Red Wings, who is not interested in a trade to a Canadian team.

On Thursday on TSN's Insider Trading , Pierre LeBrun reported that the Red Wings were actively scouting Montreal's games in case Larkin has a change of heart. Clearly, should the perfect fit become available, the Habs are still willing to make a deal.

In all of the NHL rumours that have circulated concerning the Canadiens, there has been a consistent theme. Centreman Michael Hage, currently playing for the Michigan Wolverines in the NCAA, is the first player teams will request in a trade, and is a player Hughes is unwilling to move. Seravalli confirmed Hage continues to be unavailable.

Hage is not the only young player having a good season. Alexander Zharovsky in the KHL, Luke Mittelstadt and David Reinbacher in Laval, and Adam Engstrom in Montreal are giving the Canadiens pause. They may indeed be valuable in a trade, but they may also be valuable in the lineup if Hughes were to eventually move a roster player to obtain that perfect fit.

While fans and pundits may be expecting a quick move from Hughes, Marco D'Amico, on the Starr and D'Amico Podcast on Thursday, reported that Hughes will not make a panic move to replace Suzuki based on a two to four-week absence. He said that perhaps a lateral move to bring in some help would be possible.

This take has some consistency with Seravalli's report that the Habs may be more inclined to make a Danault-like trade.

The potential for the Montreal Canadiens to make a low-key, stabilizing move is not the most exciting of NHL rumours, but it may be the smartest option for the Habs. The perfect fit may not be readily available, and young players are progressing with promise. Hughes should not be eager to trade a prospect that might be regrettable in the near future, especially when the core is so young and prospects are so close.

articles.title: Sammy Smith Wins Talladega Truck Race as Honeycutt, Riggs Keep Championship Fight Alive
articles.summary: Sammy Smith survived a chaotic afternoon at Talladega Superspeedway to win Friday’s Love’s RV Stop 225 for Spire Motorsports. Meanwhile, championship contend...
articles.body:
Sammy Smith survived a chaotic afternoon at Talladega Superspeedway to win Friday's Love's RV Stop 225 for Spire Motorsports. Meanwhile, championship contenders Kaden Honeycutt and Layne Riggs both finished in the Top 10, keeping their title battle firmly in focus.

Smith drove the No. 7 Chevrolet to victory in a race filled with shifting leaders, major incidents and late-race drama. More importantly, his victory came during a critical stretch of the NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series Chase.

However, the biggest championship takeaway belonged to Honeycutt and Riggs. Honeycutt extended his points advantage slightly, while Riggs remained within striking distance with two races left.

Smith started on the front row alongside pole-sitter Ty Majeski. From there, the race quickly developed into a typical Talladega battle, with drivers trading the lead through the draft.

These Ford teammates don't see eye to eye after @LayneRiggs99 gets shuffled on the last lap. pic.twitter.com/5Lki4zsRN5 — NASCAR CRAFTSMAN Trucks (@NASCAR_Trucks) October 23, 2026

NASCAR CRAFTSMAN Trucks (@NASCAR_Trucks) October 23, 2026

As the final stage unfolded, Honeycutt moved to the front with 29 laps remaining. Soon afterward, the leaders continued swapping positions as drivers searched for the right lane.

Smith eventually took control with 13 laps remaining. A late caution following a crash involving Thomas Annunziata and Grant Enfinger added another obstacle before Smith secured the victory.

For Spire Motorsports, the result delivered a major win on one of NASCAR's biggest stages. For Smith, it was a strong finish to an afternoon that demanded patience and precise positioning.

Honeycutt extends his championship advantage

While Smith celebrated, Honeycutt and Riggs had their own reasons to be encouraged. Both championship contenders finished inside the top 10 and avoided the kind of disastrous result that can derail a title campaign at Talladega.

Honeycutt entered the race with a 39-point advantage over Riggs. Following Friday's finish, the TRICON Garage driver increased that lead slightly.

Consequently, Honeycutt heads toward the final two races with the upper hand. Still, Riggs remains close enough to keep the championship fight alive.

The pair have separated themselves from the rest of the field throughout the Chase. Christian Eckes entered Talladega well behind the leading duo, making this increasingly a two-driver contest.

Nevertheless, Talladega demonstrated how quickly circumstances can change. One crash, mechanical issue or poorly timed pit stop can erase months of progress in a matter of seconds.

Two races remain in the championship fight

The Truck Series now moves closer to its season finale, with Martinsville Speedway and Homestead-Miami Speedway remaining on the Chase schedule.

For Honeycutt, the immediate objective is straightforward: protect the points lead and avoid costly mistakes. Riggs, meanwhile, needs to gain ground before the final race decides the championship.

Both drivers have shown they can compete at the front. Now, consistency and execution will determine who ultimately lifts the trophy.

Smith may have owned the celebration at Talladega, but the championship remains a battle between Honeycutt and Riggs. With two races remaining, the title fight is far from over.
